model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [C-FoS+Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly optimized for whole adult mouse brain clearing and deep-tissue immunolabeling. It provides excellent tissue permeability for antibodies targeting immediate early genes like C-FoS, which is essential for mapping activated neurons at single-cell resolution across all brain regions. The solvent-based clearing using DBE achieves a high refractive index (RI ~1.56), rendering the large 10 mm × 8 mm × 6 mm intact brain highly transparent for 3D light-sheet imaging while effectively preserving Alexa Fluor fluorescence.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pre-treatment and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.7 Incubation with chilled 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes methanol) for bleaching. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.8 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.9 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.10 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.11 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.12 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.13 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.14 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.15 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% Triton X-100, 20% DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.16 Incubation with blocking solution (0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 6% normal donkey serum in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

2 Immunolabeling
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody (anti-C-FoS) diluted in PTwH (PBS with 0.2% Tween-20 and 10 µg/ml heparin) containing 5% DMSO and 3% normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.2 Wash with PTwH, changing the solution 5 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor) diluted in PTwH containing 3% normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.4 Wash with PTwH, changing the solution 5 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.7 Incubation with delipidation solution consisting of 66% (vol/vol) DCM (dichloromethane) and 33% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.8 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM to wash out methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
3.9 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
3.10 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (dibenzyl ether, RI = 1.56) without shaking for refractive index matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

4 Storage and Pre-imaging Processing
4.1 Store the cleared brain in a glass vial completely filled with fresh DBE, tightly sealed and protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: Long-term)
4.2 Mount the sample in a custom 3D-printed holder or agarose block immersed in DBE immediately prior to light-sheet microscopy imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源)]
**Justification:** FDISCO is highly optimal for intact adult mouse whole brains as it provides excellent transparency while significantly preserving endogenous fluorescent proteins (like GFP). For constructing a whole-brain 3D morphological map of neuronal somas, axons, and dendrites, utilizing endogenous GFP (e.g., via transgenic labeling or viral tracing) bypasses the severe penetration limitations and long incubation times of whole-brain immunolabeling. FDISCO's low-temperature THF dehydration effectively prevents fluorescence quenching, and its solvent-based RI matching achieves the deep transparency required for whole-brain light-sheet imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Tissue Optical Clearing (Dehydration and Delipidation)
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF) aqueous solution in a glass vial with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) THF aqueous solution with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) THF aqueous solution with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) pure THF with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) pure THF with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

2 Refractive Index (RI) Matching
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI = 1.562) with gentle shaking until the tissue becomes highly transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE without shaking to ensure complete RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3 Storage and Pre-imaging Treatment
3.1 Store the cleared whole brain in fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in a dark, airtight glass vial to prevent oxidation and fluorescence decay. (Temperature: RT, Time: Long-term)
3.2 Mount the sample in a quartz cuvette or custom imaging chamber completely filled with pure DBE, allowing it to equilibrate prior to light-sheet microscopy imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.7 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.8 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.9 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.12 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.13 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (PTx.2). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.14 Incubation with permeabilization solution (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 20% DMSO, and 0.3 M glycine). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.15 Incubation with blocking solution (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, and 6% normal donkey serum). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [C-FoS+Alexa Fluor, Npas4 (IEGs)+Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** 原有简化 CUBIC 流程（仅3天）处理时间严重不足，无法实现富含髓鞘的完整成年小鼠全脑的彻底脱脂和折射率匹配，导致组织浑浊、深部信号弱且透明度不均。iDISCO+ 采用甲醇脱水和二氯甲烷（DCM）脱脂，对成年全脑具有极佳的透明化效果和抗体渗透效率，非常适合完整全脑的深层双靶点免疫荧光标记（如 C-FoS 和 Npas4 两种立即早期基因）和高分辨率三维成像。此外，iDISCO+ 处理后的样本坚硬且略微收缩，极大地便利了后续的光片显微镜全脑成像、脑区三维配准和空间聚类分析。

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pre-treatment and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
1.7 Incubation with chilled 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes methanol) for bleaching.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.8 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
1.9 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
1.10 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
1.11 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
1.12 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
1.13 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
1.14 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% Triton X-100, 20% DMSO, and 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.15 Incubation with blocking solution (0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, and 6% Donkey Serum in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

2 Whole-Brain Immunolabeling
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies (C-FoS and Npas4 (IEGs)) diluted in PTwH (PBS with 0.2% Tween-20 and 10 ug/ml heparin) containing 5% DMSO and 3% Donkey Serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 168 hours)
2.2 Wash with PTwH (change solution 5 times).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor) diluted in PTwH containing 3% Donkey Serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 168 hours)
2.4 Wash with PTwH (change solution 5 times).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
3.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
3.7 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM (dichloromethane) and 33% (vol/vol) methanol for delipidation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.8 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM to wash out methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 0.25 hours)
3.9 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM to wash out methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 0.25 hours)
3.10 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (dibenzyl ether, RI = 1.56) for refractive index matching until the brain becomes completely transparent.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** FDISCO is selected because it provides superior preservation of fluorescent proteins (like EGFP, used here for tracing long-range cortical projection fibers) by utilizing pH-adjusted tetrahydrofuran (THF) and low temperatures to prevent fluorescence quenching. It is highly effective at clearing large, lipid-rich tissues like the intact CNS (brain and spinal cord) and is fully compatible with deep whole-mount immunolabeling (e.g., β-III Tubulin) to visualize endogenous axonal networks. Additionally, the solvent-based method induces moderate tissue shrinkage, which is highly beneficial for fitting and imaging a 40 mm intact CNS under light-sheet microscopy.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pre-treatment and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with PBS to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.2 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.3 Incubation with permeabilization solution (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 20% DMSO, and 0.3 M glycine). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

2 Immunolabeling
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, and 6% Donkey Serum). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody (β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)) diluted in PTwH (PBS with 0.2% Tween-20 and 10 µg/ml heparin) containing 5% DMSO and 3% Donkey Serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 10 days)
2.3 Wash with PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, change solution 5 times)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor) diluted in PTwH containing 3% Donkey Serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 10 days)
2.5 Wash with PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours, change solution 5 times)

3 Tissue Optical Clearing (Dehydration and Delipidation)
3.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF) in ddH2O, pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) THF in ddH2O, pH adjusted to 9.0. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
3.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) THF in ddH2O, pH adjusted to 9.0. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF, pH adjusted to 9.0. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF, pH adjusted to 9.0. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
3.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF, pH adjusted to 9.0 to ensure complete dehydration and delipidation. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

4 RI Matching
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI = 1.56) without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
4.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE without shaking until the intact CNS becomes completely transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

5 Storage and Pre-imaging
5.1 Store the cleared sample in 100% DBE in a dark, airtight glass vial to prevent oxidation and fluorescence decay. (Temperature: RT, Time: Long-term)
5.2 Mount the sample in a custom 3D-printed imaging chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet microscopy, ensuring the 35-40 mm CNS is kept straight and mechanically stable. (Temperature: RT, Time: During imaging)

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pre-clearing Immunolabeling
1.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% Triton X-100, 20% DMSO in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.2 Incubation with blocking solution (0.2% Triton X-100, 10% normal donkey serum, 5% DMSO in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.3 Incubation with primary antibody against β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) diluted in blocking solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)
1.4 Wash with washing buffer (0.2% Tween-20, 10 μg/mL heparin in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
1.5 Incubation with Alexa Fluor conjugated secondary antibody diluted in blocking solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)
1.6 Wash with washing buffer (0.2% Tween-20, 10 μg/mL heparin in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

2 Tissue Optical Clearing (Decolorization and Delipidation)
2.1 Incubation with 25% (vol/vol) Quadrol aqueous solution for decolorization. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.2 Incubation with delipidation solution 1 (20% vol/vol tB-OH, 3% vol/vol Quadrol in H2O). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.3 Incubation with delipidation solution 2 (30% vol/vol tB-OH, 3% vol/vol Quadrol in H2O). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.4 Incubation with delipidation solution 3 (50% vol/vol tB-OH, 3% vol/vol Quadrol in H2O). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.5 Incubation with delipidation solution 4 (70% vol/vol tB-OH, 3% vol/vol Quadrol in H2O). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

3 Dehydration
3.1 Incubation with dehydration solution 1 (90% vol/vol tB-OH, 3% vol/vol Quadrol in H2O). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
3.2 Incubation with dehydration solution 2 (100% vol/vol tB-OH, 3% vol/vol Quadrol). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
3.3 Incubation with fresh dehydration solution 2 (100% vol/vol tB-OH, 3% vol/vol Quadrol). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

4 RI Matching and Storage
4.1 Incubation with PEGASOS clearing medium (BB-PEG: 75% vol/vol benzyl benzoate, 25% vol/vol PEG-500 monomethyl ether, RI = 1.54). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源) + Alexa Fluor, MBP + Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly suitable for large, intact lipid-rich tissues like the whole mouse CNS (brain and spinal cord, 35–40 mm) due to its powerful delipidation (DCM) and high refractive index matching (DBE), rendering heavily myelinated tracts highly transparent for light-sheet imaging. Since methanol treatment in iDISCO+ quenches endogenous fluorescence, immunolabeling against GFP is utilized to robustly amplify the anterograde projection tracer from the cortex. Co-staining with MBP (Myelin Basic Protein) provides an excellent structural reference for overall white matter tracts, allowing precise spatial localization and branching analysis of the descending EGFP-labeled axons within the brainstem and spinal cord pathways.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pretreatment and Permeabilization

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous clearing method that perfectly resolves the severe shrinkage and fluorescence quenching issues caused by harsh organic solvents. It provides excellent morphology preservation (with slight tissue expansion that aids in resolving dense projections) and is highly compatible with endogenous fluorescent proteins like GFP for long-range tracing. For the axonal reference network, whole-mount immunostaining with β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) is integrated after CUBIC-L delipidation, which acts as a powerful permeabilization step for the ultra-long intact CNS sample, enabling deep 3D imaging of both specific projections and the global axonal context.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Delipidation and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash the fixed intact CNS sample with PBS to remove excess fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
1.2 Incubation with CUBIC-L solution (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100 in water) with gentle shaking to delipidate and permeabilize the ultra-long tissue. Refresh the solution every 3 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 10 days)
1.3 Wash with PBS to remove CUBIC-L. Refresh the buffer 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

2 Whole-mount Immunostaining
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) diluted in staining buffer (PBS containing 0.5% Triton X-100, 5% normal goat serum, and 0.01% sodium azide). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.2 Wash with PBST (PBS containing 0.5% Triton X-100) to remove unbound primary antibody. Refresh the buffer 4 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody conjugated with Alexa Fluor diluted in staining buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.4 Wash with PBST to remove unbound secondary antibody. Refresh the buffer 4 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.5 Post-fixation with 1% PFA in PBS to stabilize the bound antibodies and endogenous GFP fluorophores. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
2.6 Wash with PBS to remove residual PFA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

3 Refractive Index (RI) Matching
3.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ solution (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 0.5 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, RI = 1.52, diluted in water) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-R+ solution with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
3.3 Incubation with fresh 100% CUBIC-R+ solution with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

4 Storage and Pre-imaging Preparation
4.1 Store the cleared sample in 100% CUBIC-R+ solution in a dark, airtight container until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite)
4.2 Mount the intact CNS sample in 100% CUBIC-R+ or a matched RI immersion oil (RI = 1.52) in a custom extended imaging chamber suitable for light-sheet 3D imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: During imaging)

Unlike solvent-based methods which may extract or quench small-molecule amyloid dyes during dehydration, CUBIC's mild aqueous environment ensures stable dual-target spatial cross-validation of amyloid pathology in the intact 5XFAD mouse brain.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-L (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100) in distilled water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-L with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days)
1.3 Refresh with fresh 100% CUBIC-L and continue incubation with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)

2 Wash
2.1 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
2.2 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3 Blocking and Permeabilization
3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% Donkey Serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

4 Labeling
4.1 Incubation with primary antibody 6E10 / 4G8 and Congo red in staining buffer (1% Donkey Serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
4.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
4.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
4.4 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
4.5 Incubation with Alexa Fluor secondary antibody in staining buffer (1% Donkey Serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
4.6 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
4.7 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
4.8 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 / 4G8 + Alexa Fluor, Congo red]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly effective for whole adult mouse brain clearing and immunolabeling, providing excellent transparency and tissue rigidity ideal for 3D light-sheet imaging of large samples (10×8×6 mm). The dual-target strategy combining 6E10 / 4G8 (antibody targeting the Aβ peptide sequence) and Congo red (chemical dye binding to the beta-sheet structure of amyloid fibrils) provides robust morphological and structural cross-validation. This effectively distinguishes true amyloid plaques from tissue autofluorescence or non-specific aggregates, ensuring accurate whole-brain quantification.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pretreatment and Bleaching
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.7 Incubation with chilled 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes methanol) for bleaching. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.8 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.9 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.10 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.11 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.12 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.13 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.14 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.15 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Permeabilization and Blocking
2.1 Incubation with PTx.2 (0.2% vol/vol Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with PTx.2 (0.2% vol/vol Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% vol/vol Triton X-100, 20% vol/vol DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
2.4 Incubation with blocking solution (0.2% vol/vol Triton X-100, 10% vol/vol DMSO, 6% vol/vol donkey serum in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)

3 Dual-Target Labeling
3.1 Incubation with primary antibody 6E10 / 4G8 diluted in PTwH (0.2% vol/vol Tween-20, 10 mg/ml heparin in PBS) containing 5% vol/vol DMSO and 3% vol/vol donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
3.2 Wash with PTwH, changing the solution 5 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.3 Incubation with Alexa Fluor secondary antibody and Congo red dye diluted in PTwH containing 3% vol/vol donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
3.4 Wash with PTwH, changing the solution 5 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4 Dehydration, Clearing and RI Matching
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.7 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM (dichloromethane) and 33% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
4.8 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM to remove residual methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
4.9 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
4.10 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (dibenzyl ether, RI = 1.56) without shaking until the brain becomes completely transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

5.1 Store the cleared whole brain in 100% DBE in a dark, airtight glass vial to prevent oxidation and fluorescence quenching. (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinitely)
5.2 Mount the sample in a custom 3D-printed holder or agarose block filled with DBE immediately prior to light-sheet microscopy imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous tissue clearing method that provides excellent transparency for lipid-rich brain tissue while exceptionally preserving endogenous fluorescent proteins (such as GFP in glioblastoma cells). It is highly compatible with whole-mount immunolabeling, allowing deep penetration of antibodies (like anti-CD31) into large tissue blocks (8 mm × 6 mm × 5 mm). This dual-target strategy perfectly visualizes the 3D spatial relationship between the invading tumor cells and the surrounding vascular network without quenching the endogenous tumor reporter.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Washing
1.1 Wash the fixed tissue block with PBS to remove excess fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.2 Repeat PBS wash for a total of 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Delipidation
2.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-L (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100) in dH2O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-L with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
2.3 Incubation with fresh 100% CUBIC-L with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)

3 Wash before Immunolabeling
3.1 Wash with PBS to remove CUBIC-L reagents. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.2 Repeat PBS wash for a total of 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

4 Immunolabeling
4.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
4.2 Incubation with primary antibody (anti-CD31 (PECAM1), 1:100 dilution) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days)
4.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
4.4 Repeat PBST wash for a total of 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
4.5 Incubation with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor conjugated, 1:200 dilution) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days)
4.6 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
4.7 Repeat PBST wash for a total of 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

5 Post-fixation
5.1 Incubation with 1% formaldehyde in PBS to crosslink and fix bound antibodies. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
5.2 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching
6.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 0.5% N-butyldiethanolamine, RI = 1.52) in dH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
6.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-R+ with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
6.3 Incubation with fresh 100% CUBIC-R+ with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

7 Preservation and Pre-imaging Treatment
7.1 Store the cleared sample in 100% CUBIC-R+ in the dark until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: > 24 hours)
7.2 Mount the sample in a customized imaging chamber filled with 100% CUBIC-R+ for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor, Claudin-5 + Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly effective for large, lipid-rich brain tissue blocks (8 mm × 6 mm × 5 mm) and is optimized for deep-tissue whole-mount immunolabeling. It provides high transparency and excellent antibody penetration, which is essential for mapping complex 3D vascular networks. The dual-target strategy using CD31 (pan-endothelial marker for vascular morphology) and Claudin-5 (tight junction protein for blood-brain barrier integrity) perfectly addresses the scientific goal of analyzing tumor-associated angiogenesis and barrier disruption across tumor and non-tumor regions.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pre-treatment and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.6 Incubation with chilled 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes methanol) for bleaching. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.7 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.8 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.9 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.10 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.11 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.12 Incubation with permeabilization solution containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 0.3 M glycine in PBS. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.13 Incubation with blocking solution containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 6% (vol/vol) Donkey Serum in PBS. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

2 Immunolabeling
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies (anti-CD31 and anti-Claudin-5) diluted in PTwH (PBS with 0.2% Tween-20 and 10 µg/ml Heparin) containing 5% (vol/vol) DMSO and 3% (vol/vol) Donkey Serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.2 Wash with PTwH solution, changing the solution 5 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor dyes) diluted in PTwH containing 3% (vol/vol) Donkey Serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.4 Wash with PTwH solution, changing the solution 5 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.7 Incubation with delipidation solution containing 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) and 33% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.8 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) to wash out methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
3.9 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
3.10 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) di-benzyl ether (DBE) for refractive index matching (RI = 1.56). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), Claudin-5 + Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method that avoids the severe osmotic swelling and mechanical disruption caused by aqueous methods like CUBIC, thereby perfectly preserving the fragile tumor neo-vasculature and delicate invasion boundaries in large tissue blocks. Furthermore, FDISCO utilizes low-temperature THF dehydration, which excellently preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins (unlike iDISCO+). For the dual-target strategy, endogenous GFP reliably tracks the GBM main body and invasion front without the need for deep antibody penetration. Claudin-5 is the definitive marker for endothelial tight junctions, allowing simultaneous 3D visualization of the vascular network architecture (density, branching, continuity) and the direct evaluation of Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) structural integrity.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Tissue Permeabilization and Blocking
1.1 Incubation with PBS for washing to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.2 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% vol/vol Triton X-100, 20% vol/vol DMSO in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
1.3 Incubation with blocking buffer (0.2% vol/vol Triton X-100, 10% vol/vol DMSO, 6% wt/vol Donkey Serum in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

2 Immunolabeling
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody (Claudin-5) diluted in antibody buffer (0.2% vol/vol Tween-20, 10 mg/ml heparin, 5% vol/vol DMSO, 3% wt/vol Donkey Serum in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 120 hours)
2.2 Wash with washing buffer (0.2% vol/vol Tween-20, 10 mg/ml heparin in PBS), changing buffer 5 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor) diluted in antibody buffer (0.2% vol/vol Tween-20, 10 mg/ml heparin, 3% wt/vol Donkey Serum in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 120 hours)
2.4 Wash with washing buffer (0.2% vol/vol Tween-20, 10 mg/ml heparin in PBS), changing buffer 5 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Tissue Optical Clearing (Dehydration)
3.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) THF (Tetrahydrofuran) in pH 9.0 H2O. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) THF in pH 9.0 H2O. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
3.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) THF in pH 9.0 H2O. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
3.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) THF. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

4 Refractive Index Matching and Storage

请根据该科学问题自行选择合适的双靶点荧光/标记策略，并基于所选标记样本选择匹配的组织透明方法。请仅输出 protocol，第 1 行写明所选双靶点荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** FDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), DAPI]
**Justification:** FDISCO is specifically selected because it is a solvent-based clearing method that provides excellent transparency for 3 mm brain blocks while uniquely utilizing low temperature (4 ℃) and alkaline pH adjustment (pH 9.0 via TEA) during dehydration. This specifically prevents the quenching of weak endogenous fluorescent proteins (like GFP), allowing for high-resolution 3D morphological analysis of fine dendritic structures and long-term storage (months) without signal loss. The dual-target strategy utilizes the preserved endogenous GFP to trace sparse neurons, while DAPI serves as a nuclear counterstain to provide essential 3D anatomical context without requiring complex immunolabeling that might damage the tissue.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Sample Pre-treatment and Labeling
1.1 Incubation with 1x PBS to remove residual fixative.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.2 Incubation with DAPI (10 µg/mL) in 1x PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
1.3 Incubation with 1x PBS to wash out excess DAPI dye.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

2 Dehydration
2.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) THF aqueous solution (pH adjusted to 9.0 with TEA).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)
2.2 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) THF aqueous solution (pH adjusted to 9.0 with TEA).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)
2.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) THF aqueous solution (pH adjusted to 9.0 with TEA).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)
2.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF (pH adjusted to 9.0 with TEA).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)
2.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) THF (pH adjusted to 9.0 with TEA).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

3 Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Refractive Index = 1.56) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

4 Storage and Pre-imaging
4.1 Store the cleared sample immersed in 100% (vol/vol) DBE in a dark, airtight glass vial to maintain transparency and preserve endogenous fluorescence.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Long-term)
4.2 Mount the sample in 100% (vol/vol) DBE for 3D light-sheet or confocal imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** FDISCO is specifically optimized to preserve weak endogenous fluorescence (such as GFP) and allows for long-term storage (over 6 months) without significant signal quenching. It achieves this by utilizing low temperature (4 ℃) and alkaline pH (9.0) during the dehydration process, which minimizes fluorescence loss and tissue deformation compared to standard solvent-based methods. It provides excellent transparency for thick (3 mm) brain tissues. Combining the endogenous sparse GFP signal with MAP2 immunolabeling (visualized via Alexa Fluor) effectively highlights the reporter neurons while fully reconstructing dendritic morphology, preventing the loss of fine structural details during clearing.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Permeabilization and Blocking
1.1 Wash the fixed 3 mm brain tissue block with PBS to remove residual fixative.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with permeabilization solution (PBS containing 0.2% vol/vol Triton X-100, 20% vol/vol DMSO, and 0.3 M glycine).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (PBS containing 0.2% vol/vol Triton X-100, 10% vol/vol DMSO, and 6% vol/vol normal donkey serum).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

2 Immunolabeling
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody against MAP2 diluted in washing buffer (PBS containing 0.2% vol/vol Tween-20 and 10 μg/mL heparin) supplemented with 5% vol/vol DMSO and 3% vol/vol normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.2 Wash with washing buffer (PBS containing 0.2% vol/vol Tween-20 and 10 μg/mL heparin), changing the buffer every 4 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor) diluted in washing buffer supplemented with 3% vol/vol normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.4 Wash with washing buffer, changing the buffer every 4 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 FDISCO Dehydration
3.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) THF aqueous solution (pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) THF aqueous solution (pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)
3.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) THF aqueous solution (pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF (pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)
3.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) THF (pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)

4 RI Matching and Clearing
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Dibenzyl ether, RI = 1.562) in a glass vial.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
4.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE until the tissue becomes completely transparent.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

5 Long-term Storage and Pre-imaging Treatment
5.1 Store the cleared sample immersed in 100% DBE in a dark, airtight glass vial to prevent oxidation and fluorescence quenching.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 6 months)
5.2 Before 3D imaging, equilibrate the sample vial to room temperature to avoid refractive index mismatch and optical aberrations caused by temperature gradients.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源) + Alexa Fluor, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** FDISCO is specifically optimized to preserve fluorescence (including weak endogenous signals and synthetic dyes) for long-term storage (over 6 months) by using low-temperature dehydration and pH-adjusted solvents. For a 3 mm thick brain block, FDISCO provides excellent transparency and slight tissue hardening, which is ideal for repeated handling and imaging. To address the weak endogenous signal and the need for dendritic/local circuit analysis, a dual-target immunolabeling strategy is chosen: amplifying the sparse endogenous GFP with an Alexa Fluor secondary antibody, and co-labeling MAP2 with a different Alexa Fluor to visualize the detailed dendritic skeleton and local neuronal structures.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Permeabilization and Blocking
1.1 Wash the fixed tissue block with 1x PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% vol/vol Triton X-100, 20% vol/vol DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.3 Incubation with blocking buffer (0.2% vol/vol Triton X-100, 10% vol/vol DMSO, 6% vol/vol donkey serum in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

2 Dual-Target Immunolabeling
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies (anti-GFP and anti-MAP2) diluted in antibody buffer (0.2% vol/vol Tween-20, 10 mg/ml heparin, 5% vol/vol DMSO, 3% vol/vol donkey serum in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.2 Wash with washing buffer (0.2% vol/vol Tween-20, 10 mg/ml heparin in PBS), changing the buffer every 4-6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647) diluted in antibody buffer (0.2% vol/vol Tween-20, 10 mg/ml heparin, 3% vol/vol donkey serum in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.4 Wash with washing buffer (0.2% vol/vol Tween-20, 10 mg/ml heparin in PBS), changing the buffer every 4-6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Tissue Optical Clearing (FDISCO Dehydration)
3.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) THF (tetrahydrofuran, pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine) in distilled water. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) THF (pH adjusted to 9.0) in distilled water. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
3.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) THF (pH adjusted to 9.0) in distilled water. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF (pH adjusted to 9.0). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
3.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) THF (pH adjusted to 9.0). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

5 Long-term Storage and Pre-imaging Treatment

**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, MAP2+Alexa Fluor]

As a solvent-based method, it provides superior clearing efficacy for 3 mm thick tissue blocks and allows for highly stable long-term storage (over 6 months) in DBE without signal decay. To address the potential loss of dendritic details from the sparse and weak endogenous reporter, MAP2 is selected to robustly label the neuronal cytoskeleton and dendrites, paired with highly stable Alexa Fluor dyes, ensuring complete 3D morphological reconstruction of the neurons.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Immunolabeling
1.1 Wash the fixed tissue block with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation for permeabilization with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 0.3 M glycine in PBS. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.3 Incubation for blocking with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum in PBS. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.4 Incubation with primary antibody (anti-MAP2, 1:200) in PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10 mg/ml heparin, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 3% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
1.5 Wash with PTwH (PBS containing 0.2% Tween-20 and 10 mg/ml heparin), changing the solution every 4-6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
1.6 Incubation with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor conjugated, 1:400) in PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10 mg/ml heparin, and 3% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
1.7 Wash with PTwH, changing the solution every 4-6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

2 Tissue Optical Clearing (Dehydration)
2.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) THF (Tetrahydrofuran) aqueous solution, pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
2.2 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) THF aqueous solution, pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
2.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) THF aqueous solution, pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
2.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF, pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
2.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) THF, pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

3 Refractive Index (RI) Matching

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3)+Alexa Fluor, MAP2+Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly effective for dense, highly myelinated, and lipid-rich adult human brain tissue. The methanol and dichloromethane (DCM) pretreatment provides robust delipidation, while the 5% H2O2 step significantly reduces human tissue autofluorescence. The previous failure (1 mm penetration) was due to using PBS at 4 ℃ for only 72 hours; iDISCO+ solves this by utilizing specialized permeabilization buffers (containing DMSO, Triton X-100, and Heparin) and elevating the incubation temperature to 37 ℃ for extended periods (7 days per antibody), ensuring full penetration through the 3 mm thickness. NeuN (nuclei) and MAP2 (soma/dendrites) are selected as the dual mature neuron markers to provide comprehensive and reliable 3D cellular identification across the cortical layers.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pre-treatment and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.8 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.9 Incubation with chilled 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes methanol) for bleaching. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

1.13 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.14 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.15 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Justification:** FDISCO is highly efficient for 500 μm thick brain slices, allowing complete dehydration and clearing within 6-8 hours, strictly meeting the 1-day (24h) constraint. DAPI provides rapid nuclear counterstaining for anatomical layer identification without requiring lengthy antibody incubation. The final clearing in DBE provides a high refractive index (RI ~1.56), minimizing spherical aberration and enabling high-resolution confocal or light-sheet imaging of dendritic spines deep within the thick tissue.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Labeling and Counterstaining
1.1 Incubation with 10 μg/mL DAPI in 0.01 M PBS to counterstain nuclei. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Dehydration
2.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF, pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine) in distilled water. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) THF (pH 9.0) in distilled water. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) THF (pH 9.0) in distilled water. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF (pH 9.0). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
2.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) THF (pH 9.0). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)

3 RI Matching and Clearing
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI = 1.562) without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Preservation and Pre-imaging Processing
4.1 Transfer and store the cleared sample in fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in a dark, glass vial to stabilize the refractive index prior to imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** FOCM
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** FOCM (Fast Optical Clearing Method) is an ultra-fast, aqueous clearing technique perfectly suited for 500 μm brain slices, achieving complete transparency and refractive index matching in under an hour, strictly satisfying the 1-day clearing constraint. It excellently preserves weak endogenous fluorescence (like GFP) without quenching, which is critical for high-resolution imaging of fine dendritic spines. For the dual-target strategy, endogenous GFP provides the sparse labeling of pyramidal neurons to resolve spines, while immunolabeling with MAP2 and Alexa Fluor visualizes the main dendritic skeleton. This combination allows for accurate spine density counting and dendritic length normalization.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pre-treatment and Immunolabeling
1.1 Incubation with permeabilization and blocking buffer (5% Normal Goat Serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) to block non-specific binding and permeabilize the 500 μm thick slice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody against MAP2 diluted in the permeabilization and blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 3 times to remove unbound primary antibodies. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor) diluted in the permeabilization and blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.5 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 3 times to remove unbound secondary antibodies. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)
1.6 Wash with standard PBS to remove excess detergent prior to optical clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

2 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
2.1 Incubation with FOCM solution (30% wt/vol urea, 20% wt/vol D-sorbitol, 5% wt/vol glycerol dissolved in a 1:3 vol/vol mixture of DMSO and distilled water, RI ≈ 1.43 - 1.44) with gentle shaking until the slice becomes completely transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3 Storage and Pre-imaging Preparation
3.1 Mount the cleared brain slice on a glass slide with a spacer (e.g., silicone gasket) to accommodate the 500 μm thickness, immersed in a drop of fresh FOCM solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)
3.2 Cover with a coverslip and seal the edges tightly with nail polish or a compatible sealant to prevent evaporation and sample drying during high-resolution confocal or light-sheet imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
3.3 Store the prepared slides in the dark to protect the endogenous GFP and Alexa Fluor signals until imaging. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to several weeks)

**Chosen Method:** SeeDB2
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, F-Actin+Phalloidin+Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** SeeDB2 is specifically optimized for high-resolution quantitative imaging of fine structures like dendritic spines. It perfectly preserves tissue volume (no shrinkage or swelling) and endogenous fluorescence (such as EGFP). By matching the refractive index to 1.52, it minimizes spherical aberration for high-NA objectives, which is critical for spine identification. The step-by-step Omnipaque gradient can clear a 500 μm slice within 12 hours, easily fitting the 1-day requirement. Using endogenous EGFP provides the dendritic backbone reference, while Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor rapidly and specifically labels F-actin (which is highly enriched in dendritic spines), enabling precise spine identification and density quantification within a short experimental cycle.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Tissue Permeabilization and Washing
1.1 Wash the fixed 500 μm brain slice with 1x PBS to remove residual fixative.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 mins)
1.2 Incubation with 2% (wt/vol) saponin in 1x PBS for deep permeabilization.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Fluorescent Labeling
2.1 Incubation with Phalloidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor diluted in 1x PBS containing 2% (wt/vol) saponin.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
2.2 Wash with 1x PBS to remove unbound Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 mins)
2.3 Wash with 1x PBS for a second time.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 mins)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** SeeDB2
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), F-Actin+Phalloidin+Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** The previous failure was caused by methanol fixation (which quenches endogenous fluorescence and destroys lipid structures) and direct immersion in 100% TDE (which causes severe osmotic shock and tissue shrinkage, blurring fine structures). SeeDB2 is specifically designed for high-resolution imaging of dendritic spines with near-zero deformation, matching the refractive index of oil-immersion objectives (RI=1.52). To meet the 1-day processing constraint and complete the dendritic skeleton, slow antibody staining is replaced with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor. Phalloidin is a small molecule that rapidly penetrates 300-500 μm slices to specifically label F-actin (highly enriched in dendritic spines), perfectly highlighting spine morphology alongside the sparsely labeled endogenous GFP.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash the PFA-fixed brain slices (strictly avoid methanol fixation) in PBS to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
1.2 Incubation with 2% (wt/vol) saponin in PBS for deep tissue permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Fluorescent Labeling
2.1 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor in PBS containing 2% (wt/vol) saponin to rapidly label F-actin in dendritic spines and skeleton. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
2.2 Wash with PBS to remove excess unbound dye. (Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)
2.3 Wash with PBS again to ensure minimal background fluorescence. (Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)

3 Optical Clearing and RI Matching
3.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) SeeDB2G (Omnipaque 350 diluted in water supplemented with 0.1% saponin). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 100% SeeDB2G (Omnipaque 350, RI = 1.52, supplemented with 0.1% saponin). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.3 Incubation with fresh 100% SeeDB2G to ensure complete refractive index matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

4 Storage and Pre-imaging Processing
4.1 Mount the cleared brain slice in fresh 100% SeeDB2G on a glass slide with a spacer (e.g., 300-500 μm thickness) to prevent physical compression, and seal with a coverslip for high-resolution imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)+Alexa Fluor, PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly optimized for whole-mount immunolabeling and optical clearing of intact mouse embryos (E12.5, 8-10 mm). It provides deep antibody penetration and excellent transparency for dense tissues, which is essential for tracing long-distance nerve projections. The dual-target strategy using β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) and PGP9.5 (both robust pan-neuronal markers) ensures comprehensive and highly reliable labeling of all early developing cranial, spinal, and peripheral nerve tracts, minimizing false negatives during 3D reconstruction.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pre-treatment and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.7 Incubation with chilled 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes methanol) for bleaching. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.8 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.9 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.10 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.11 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.12 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.13 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.14 Incubation with permeabilization solution (PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 20% DMSO, and 0.3 M glycine). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

2 Immunolabeling
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, and 6% normal donkey serum). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies (β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) and PGP9.5) diluted in PTwH (PBS with 0.2% Tween-20 and 10 µg/ml heparin) containing 5% DMSO and 3% normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.3 Wash with PTwH, changing the solution every 4-5 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor dyes) diluted in PTwH containing 3% normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.5 Wash with PTwH, changing the solution every 4-5 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.7 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) and 33% (vol/vol) methanol for delipidation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.8 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM to wash out methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
3.9 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
3.10 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI = 1.56) for refractive index matching and storage prior to imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

The dual-target combination of β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) and PGP9.5 provides robust, comprehensive labeling of both early delicate neurites and mature nerve bundles. 2.2 Incubation with permeabilization solution (PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 20% DMSO, and 0.3 M glycine) to facilitate deep tissue penetration. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) + Alexa Fluor 488, Synapsin + Alexa Fluor 594]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly effective for insect samples containing chitinous cuticles, as its solvent-based RI matching (using DBE, RI ~ 1.56) closely matches the high refractive index of the cuticle, minimizing light scattering. The methanol and H2O2 pre-treatment steps efficiently bleach Drosophila eye pigments and reduce cuticle autofluorescence. Alexa Fluor dyes are robust in organic solvents, ensuring strong, stable signals for resolving presynaptic active zones (BRP) and synaptic vesicles (Synapsin) during high-resolution 3D imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pre-treatment and Pigment Bleaching (Cuticle Background Processing)
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.6 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes methanol) to bleach eye pigments and cuticle. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.8 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.9 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.10 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.11 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.12 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Tissue Optical Clearing (Post-Immunolabeling Dehydration and Delipidation)
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.7 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) and 33% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.8 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM to complete delipidation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for final clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

4 Storage and Pre-imaging Preparation
4.1 Store the cleared sample in 100% DBE in a dark, airtight glass vial. (Temperature: RT, Time: Long-term)
4.2 Mount the sample in a glass-bottom chamber or custom holder filled with 100% DBE, ensuring no air bubbles are trapped near the cuticle. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)

Using Alexa Fluor secondary antibodies ensures high photostability and brightness, which is essential for resolving the spatial correspondence between active zones and vesicle domains in 3D at high resolution.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Depigmentation and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) H2O2 in 0.5% PBST (PBS with 0.5% Triton X-100) to bleach the pigmented cuticle. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.2 Wash with 0.5% PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) DMSO in 0.5% PBST to enhance tissue permeability. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.4 Wash with 0.5% PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Immunolabeling
2.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% Normal Goat Serum in 0.5% PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies (anti-Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) and anti-Synapsin, 1:100 dilution) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.3 Wash with 0.5% PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 594, 1:200 dilution) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.5 Wash with 0.5% PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

3 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
3.1 Incubation with 25% (vol/vol) FlyClear solution (Histodenz-based, RI = 1.52) in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) FlyClear solution in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.3 Incubation with 75% (vol/vol) FlyClear solution in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.4 Incubation with 100% FlyClear solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
3.5 Incubation with fresh 100% FlyClear solution for final refractive index matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

4 Storage and Pre-imaging Preparation
4.1 Mount the cleared sample in fresh 100% FlyClear solution within a customized imaging chamber. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)
4.2 Store the mounted sample in the dark until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite)

4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix) + Alexa Fluor, Osteocalcin + Alexa Fluor, DAPI]
**Justification:** PEGASOS is highly optimized for hard tissues like bones and skulls. It incorporates an EDTA decalcification step that renders calcified tissues highly transparent while excellently preserving the fluorescence of organic dyes (Alexa Fluor) and nuclear stains (DAPI). Using Osx (Osterix) and Osteocalcin allows for the precise spatial differentiation of committed osteoprogenitors/early osteoblasts from mature osteoblasts, perfectly addressing the scientific goal of mapping the osteogenic lineage in the P7 skull suture.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Decalcification
1.1 Incubation with 20% (wt/vol) EDTA aqueous solution (pH 7.4) with gentle shaking to decalcify the skull plate. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.2 Wash with PBS to remove excess EDTA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

2 Immunolabeling
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization and blocking buffer (PBS containing 0.5% Triton X-100 and 5% normal donkey serum). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies (anti-Osx and anti-Osteocalcin) diluted in the blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBST (PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20) with multiple changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor conjugated) and DAPI diluted in the blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.5 Wash with PBST (PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20) with multiple changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3 Decolorization
3.1 Incubation with 25% (vol/vol) Quadrol aqueous solution with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

4 Delipidation and Dehydration
4.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) tert-butanol (tB) aqueous solution containing 3% (wt/vol) Quadrol. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
4.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) tert-butanol (tB) aqueous solution containing 3% (wt/vol) Quadrol. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
4.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) tert-butanol (tB) aqueous solution containing 3% (wt/vol) Quadrol. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
4.4 Incubation with tB-PEG solution (70% vol/vol tert-butanol, 27% vol/vol PEG-500M, 3% wt/vol Quadrol). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

5 Clearing and RI Matching
5.1 Incubation with BB-PEG solution (75% vol/vol benzyl benzoate, 22% vol/vol PEG-500M, 3% wt/vol Quadrol, RI = 1.54). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

6 Storage and Pre-imaging Processing
6.1 Store the cleared skull sample in fresh BB-PEG solution in a dark, airtight container to prevent fluorescence quenching and evaporation. (Temperature: RT, Time: Long-term)
6.2 Mount the sample immersed in BB-PEG solution within a custom imaging chamber or agarose well suitable for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix) + Alexa Fluor 488, Osteocalcin + Alexa Fluor 647]
**Justification:** PEGASOS is specifically optimized for hard tissues like bone, providing excellent transparency while using PEG-500 mMA to prevent severe tissue shrinkage, ensuring low deformation. Osx (Osterix) is a classic marker for early osteoprogenitors, and Osteocalcin specifically labels mature osteoblasts. 1.4 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies (anti-Osx and anti-Osteocalcin) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** PEGASOS is highly optimized for intact hard tissues like adult mouse bones. It incorporates an efficient EDTA-based decalcification step and uses polyethylene glycol (PEG) to protect fluorescence during solvent-based clearing. This method provides excellent transparency for the highly scattering bone matrix and marrow while maintaining low tissue deformation, which is critical for the accurate 3D spatial quantification, distance measurement, and overlap analysis of sympathetic nerves (TH) and vascular niches (CD31) in the hematopoietic stem cell microenvironment.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Decalcification and Decolorization
1.1 Incubation with 20% (wt/vol) EDTA aqueous solution (pH 7.4) with gentle shaking to decalcify the intact femur. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days)
1.2 Wash with PBS to remove excess EDTA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
1.3 Incubation with decolorization solution containing 25% (vol/vol) Quadrol and 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in PBS. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
1.4 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

2 Immunolabeling
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization and blocking buffer (10% vol/vol normal donkey serum, 0.5% vol/vol Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies (TH and CD31 (PECAM1)) diluted in the permeabilization and blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)
2.3 Wash with washing buffer (0.2% vol/vol Tween-20, 10 µg/mL heparin in PBS) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor) diluted in the permeabilization and blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)
2.5 Wash with washing buffer (0.2% vol/vol Tween-20, 10 µg/mL heparin in PBS) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day)

3 Delipidation and Dehydration
3.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) tert-butanol (tB-OH) and 3% (vol/vol) Quadrol in distilled water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 day)
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) tB-OH and 3% (vol/vol) Quadrol in distilled water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 day)
3.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) tB-OH and 3% (vol/vol) Quadrol in distilled water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 day)
3.4 Incubation with 97% (vol/vol) tB-OH and 3% (vol/vol) Quadrol in distilled water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 day)
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tB-OH and 3% (vol/vol) Quadrol. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 day)

4 Refractive Index Matching and Pre-imaging
4.1 Incubation with BB-PEG clearing medium (75% vol/vol benzyl benzoate, 25% vol/vol PEG-500 methyl ether, 3% vol/vol Quadrol, RI = 1.54). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
4.2 Storage and pre-imaging incubation in fresh BB-PEG clearing medium prior to light-sheet or confocal imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** PEGASOS is specifically designed for hard tissues like bone. By incorporating polyethylene glycol (PEG) into the tert-butanol dehydration gradient and the clearing medium, PEG acts as a plasticizer. This effectively prevents the severe tissue brittleness and fragmentation associated with pure tert-butanol (as seen in BoneClear), thereby preserving the spatial continuity of the bone marrow cavity. TH and CD31 (PECAM1) are classic, robust markers for sympathetic nerves and vascular endothelial cells, respectively, perfectly matching the scientific goals of dual-signal detection in the microenvironment.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Dehydration and Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) tert-butanol (tBuOH) containing 3% (wt/vol) PEG-400 and 3% (wt/vol) Quadrol in distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) tBuOH containing 3% (wt/vol) PEG-400 and 3% (wt/vol) Quadrol in distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) tBuOH containing 3% (wt/vol) PEG-400 and 3% (wt/vol) Quadrol in distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.4 Incubation with 90% (vol/vol) tBuOH containing 3% (wt/vol) PEG-400 and 3% (wt/vol) Quadrol in distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tBuOH containing 3% (wt/vol) PEG-400 and 3% (wt/vol) Quadrol with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) tBuOH containing 3% (wt/vol) PEG-400 and 3% (wt/vol) Quadrol with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2 Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
2.1 Incubation with BB-PEG clearing medium (75% vol/vol benzyl benzoate, 22% vol/vol PEGDMA-500, 3% wt/vol Quadrol, RI = 1.54) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with fresh BB-PEG clearing medium with gentle shaking until the femur becomes completely transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Preservation and Pre-imaging Preparation
3.1 Store the cleared femur in fresh BB-PEG clearing medium in a dark, airtight container to preserve fluorescence and tissue flexibility. (Temperature: RT, Time: Long-term)
3.2 Mount the sample in a quartz cuvette or imaging chamber completely filled with BB-PEG clearing medium for 3D light-sheet or confocal imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: During imaging)

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin, DAPI]
**Justification:** The mouse cochlea is deeply encased in the dense bone of the tympanic bulla. PEGASOS is specifically designed for hard tissues and bone clearing, utilizing an efficient EDTA decalcification step followed by a PEG-associated solvent system that renders bone highly transparent while preventing tissue shrinkage and preserving the delicate spiral architecture. According to the restrictions, since F-actin is highly enriched in the stereocilia of inner and outer hair cells, the small-molecule fluorescent probe Phalloidin can directly and specifically label the hair cell bundles without the need for antibodies. DAPI is included as a nuclear counterstain to provide spatial and anatomical reference for the sensory epithelium.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Decalcification
1.1 Incubation with 20% (w/v) EDTA aqueous solution (pH 7.4) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

2 Washing
2.1 Wash with 1x PBS to remove excess EDTA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Fluorescent Labeling
3.1 Incubation with Phalloidin (fluorophore-conjugated) and DAPI in 1x PBS containing 0.5% (v/v) Triton X-100. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

4 Washing
4.1 Wash with 1x PBS to remove unbound dyes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

5 Decolorization
5.1 Incubation with 25% (v/v) Quadrol aqueous solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

6 Delipidation and Dehydration
6.1 Incubation with 30% (v/v) tert-Butanol (tBA) containing 3% (w/v) Quadrol. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
6.2 Incubation with 50% (v/v) tert-Butanol (tBA) containing 3% (w/v) Quadrol. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
6.3 Incubation with 70% (v/v) tert-Butanol (tBA) containing 3% (w/v) Quadrol. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
6.4 Incubation with 100% (v/v) tert-Butanol (tBA) containing 3% (w/v) Quadrol. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
6.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (v/v) tert-Butanol (tBA) containing 3% (w/v) Quadrol. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

7 Clearing and RI Matching
7.1 Incubation with BB-PEG clearing medium (75% v/v benzyl benzoate, 25% v/v PEG-500 methacrylate, 3% w/v Quadrol, RI = 1.543). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

8 Storage and Pre-imaging
8.1 Store the cleared sample in BB-PEG clearing medium in a dark, sealed container. (Temperature: RT, Time: Long-term)
8.2 Mount the sample in fresh BB-PEG clearing medium within a customized imaging chamber prior to 3D light-sheet or confocal imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1 Delipidation and Decalcification
1.1 Wash fixed cochlea samples with PBS to remove residual fixative.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 times, 1 hour each)

By incorporating an EDTA decalcification step, CUBIC effectively clears the hard bone of the auditory bulla while maintaining the delicate spiral structure of the cochlea. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin to assess stereocilia bundle disruption, while Myosin VIIa immunolabeling allows for precise 3D mapping and automated counting of hair cells.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Decalcification
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA aqueous solution (pH 7.4) with gentle shaking to decalcify the dense auditory bulla bone. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
1.2 Wash with PBS (1X) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.3 Wash with PBS (1X) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.4 Wash with PBS (1X) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Delipidation
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100 in water) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.2 Wash with PBS (1X) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBS (1X) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.4 Wash with PBS (1X) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Immunolabeling and Dye Staining
3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody Myosin VIIa (diluted 1:200 in blocking buffer) to label hair cells. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
3.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.4 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.5 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.6 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor (1:500), Phalloidin (1:200, for F-actin/stereocilia), and DAPI (1:1000, for nuclei) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
3.7 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.8 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.9 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

5.1 Store the cleared cochlea sample in 100% CUBIC-R+ in a dark container until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
