**Chosen Method:** CUBIC
**Chosen Labeling:** [HuC/D+Alexa Fluor, PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor, Phalloidin+Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous clearing method highly suitable for gastrointestinal tissues. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+) that severely quench or destroy F-actin structures, CUBIC preserves the binding capability of Phalloidin, allowing it to be used as a robust structural reference for the intestinal muscle layers (circular and longitudinal). Combined with HuC/D (neuronal soma) and PGP9.5 (nerve fibers), this aqueous approach ensures deep antibody penetration through the 3 mm thick tubular colon while achieving high transparency for 3D mapping of the enteric nervous system.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Delipidation and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L solution (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100 in dH2O) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
1.2 Wash with PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.3 Wash with PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.4 Wash with PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Immunolabeling and F-actin Staining
2.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies (anti-HuC/D and anti-PGP9.5) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days)
2.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.4 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.5 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.6 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor) and Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days)
2.7 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.8 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.9 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Post-fixation (Phalloidin Stabilization)
3.1 Incubation with 4% PFA in PBS to crosslink and stabilize Phalloidin binding before RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.2 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching
4.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ solution (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 0.5 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine in dH2O) diluted in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
4.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-R+ solution with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
4.3 Incubation with fresh 100% CUBIC-R+ solution with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

5 Storage and Pre-imaging Preparation
5.1 Store the cleared colon sample in fresh 100% CUBIC-R+ solution in the dark until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: > 12 hours)
5.2 Mount the sample in 100% CUBIC-R+ (RI = 1.52) using an agarose mold or custom chamber suitable for light-sheet or confocal imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly effective for dense, intact tissues like the mouse eyeball. Its standard protocol includes a robust methanol/H2O2 bleaching step, which is absolutely critical for eliminating melanin in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) to achieve complete transparency. It is highly compatible with whole-mount immunolabeling for retinal ganglion cells (using β-III Tubulin/TUJ1) and direct vascular lumen labeling (using IB4), followed by refractive index matching in DBE for high-resolution 3D imaging of the intact structure.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pretreatment and Melanin Bleaching
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.6 Incubation with chilled 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes methanol) for melanin bleaching. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.8 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.9 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.10 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.11 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.12 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.13 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Permeabilization and Immunolabeling
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 20% DMSO, and 23 g/L glycine). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, and 6% normal donkey serum). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.3 Incubation with primary antibody β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) and IB4 diluted in washing buffer (PBS with 0.2% Tween-20, 10 µg/mL heparin, 5% DMSO, 3% normal donkey serum). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.4 Wash with washing buffer (PBS with 0.2% Tween-20 and 10 µg/mL heparin), changing buffer every 4-6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.5 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor) diluted in washing buffer with 3% normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.6 Wash with washing buffer, changing buffer every 4-6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.9 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

4.2 Mount the sample in a glass imaging chamber filled with fresh 100% DBE prior to light-sheet or confocal imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)

For labeling, using both HuC/D and Tuj1 allows for the required cross-validation of retinal ganglion cell identity, while Lectin effectively stains the vascular lumen network. 1 Delipidation and Depigmentation
1.1 Wash with PBS to remove excess fixative.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-L (diluted in distilled water) for initial delipidation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.3 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-L (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100) for thorough delipidation, change solution once.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days)
1.4 Wash with PBS to remove CUBIC-L, 3 solution changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.5 Incubation with 3% H2O2 in PBS for depigmentation and bleaching of the RPE pigment layer.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
1.6 Wash with PBS to remove residual H2O2, 3 solution changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies (HuC/D and Tuj1) and Lectin diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)

2.5 Wash with PBST (PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100), 4 solution changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

Ki67 (MKI67) paired with Alexa Fluor is selected to specifically label and assess the spatial distribution of proliferating cells, directly addressing the need to monitor growth inhibition and reduced proliferation zones.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pre-clearing Fluorescent Labeling
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 for permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

1.3 Incubation with primary antibody against Ki67 (MKI67) (1:200 dilution) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.4 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 for washing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.5 Incubation with Alexa Fluor secondary antibody (1:500 dilution) and DAPI (5 µg/mL) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.6 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 for washing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
2.1 Incubation with FOCM solution (30% wt/vol urea, 20% wt/vol D-sorbitol, 5% wt/vol glycerol in DMSO/water mixture, RI = 1.43). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.2 Incubation with fresh FOCM solution for complete clearing and refractive index matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3 Storage and Pre-imaging Treatment
3.1 Mount the cleared organoids in fresh FOCM solution within a glass-bottom imaging chamber. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
3.2 Store the mounted samples in the dark prior to high-throughput imaging. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC
**Chosen Labeling:** [DAPI, Ki67 (MKI67) + Alexa Fluor, PCNA + Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** CUBIC is highly compatible with 1–3 mm 3D human brain organoids, providing excellent transparency while preserving tissue morphology and avoiding the severe shrinkage associated with solvent-based methods. It perfectly preserves the fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes and DAPI. The aqueous nature of CUBIC allows for efficient penetration of antibodies for multiplexed immunostaining of proliferation markers (Ki67 for cell cycle progression and PCNA for DNA replication) deep within the organoids. This enables the precise 3D evaluation of proliferating cell ratios, spatial distribution, and central proliferation deficits required for high-throughput drug toxicity screening.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Tissue Preparation and Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS for fixation.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.2 Wash with 1x PBS for 3 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes each)
1.3 Incubation with CUBIC-L solution (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100 in dH2O) for delipidation and permeabilization.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.4 Wash with 1x PBS for 3 times to remove CUBIC-L.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)

2 Immunostaining (Labeling)
2.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Ki67 (MKI67) and anti-PCNA diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 3 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor conjugated) and DAPI (5 µg/mL) diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.5 Wash with PBST for 3 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)
2.6 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS for post-fixation to stabilize bound antibodies.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.7 Wash with 1x PBS for 3 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes each)

3 Refractive Index (RI) Matching and Clearing
3.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ solution (diluted with dH2O; 100% CUBIC-R+ contains 45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 0.5 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, RI = 1.52).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-R+ solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.3 Incubation with fresh 100% CUBIC-R+ solution for final clearing.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4 Storage and Pre-imaging Treatment
4.1 Store the cleared organoids in 100% CUBIC-R+ solution in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: Long-term)
4.2 Mount the organoids in a multi-well plate or agarose mold filled with 100% CUBIC-R+ solution for high-throughput imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)

It is an aqueous method that excellently preserves fluorescence and requires minimal steps. DAPI is chosen to label total nuclei for assessing cell density and central necrosis. It perfectly preserves fluorescence, making it ideal for high-throughput screening. The labeling strategy uses Ki67 and PCNA to simultaneously assess cell cycle and DNA replication, while Hoechst and Phalloidin provide nuclear and structural boundaries to evaluate organoid volume and integrity.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Tissue Permeabilization and Blocking
1.1 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
1.2 Incubation with blocking buffer containing 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum and 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

2 Immunolabeling and Structural Staining
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies against Ki67 (MKI67) and PCNA diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Wash with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (PBST) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
2.3 Incubation with Alexa Fluor-conjugated secondary antibodies, Alexa Fluor-conjugated Phalloidin (for F-Actin), and Hoechst diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.4 Wash with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (PBST) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

3 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
3.1 Incubation with FOCM solution (30% wt/vol urea, 20% wt/vol D-sorbitol, and 5% wt/vol glycerol in a 1:3 vol/vol mixture of DMSO and water, RI = 1.43 - 1.44). (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

4 Storage and Pre-imaging Preparation
4.1 Mount the cleared organoids in fresh FOCM solution in high-throughput imaging microplates. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)
4.2 Store the microplates protected from light until imaging. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Long-term)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [DAPI, PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor, CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** Human skin biopsy tissues are highly scattering and rich in collagen and melanin, making them difficult to clear. iDISCO+ is chosen because its solvent-based dehydration and delipidation (using methanol and DCM) provide aggressive permeabilization and excellent transparency for dense, tough tissues. The protocol includes a crucial bleaching step to reduce melanin pigment and autofluorescence. PGP9.5 is the gold-standard marker for identifying intraepidermal nerve fibers (IENF), CD31 labels the superficial dermal blood vessels to help delineate the dermal papillae structure, and DAPI provides a robust nuclear reference for epidermal thickness and cellular layers.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pre-treatment and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash with 1x PBS to remove fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Dehydration with 20% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Dehydration with 40% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Dehydration with 60% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Dehydration with 80% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.6 Dehydration with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.7 Dehydration with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.8 Delipidation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) and 33% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.9 Delipidation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
1.10 Bleaching with chilled fresh 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes methanol) to reduce melanin and autofluorescence. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.11 Rehydration with 80% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.12 Rehydration with 60% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.13 Rehydration with 40% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.14 Rehydration with 20% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.15 Wash with 1x PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.16 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PTx.2). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.17 Permeabilization with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 0.3 M glycine. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.18 Blocking with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 6% (vol/vol) donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

2 Immunolabeling
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies (PGP9.5 and CD31 (PECAM1)) in PTwH buffer (PBS with 0.2% Tween-20 and 10 µg/ml heparin) containing 5% (vol/vol) DMSO and 3% (vol/vol) donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.2 Wash with PTwH buffer, changing the buffer every 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor) and DAPI in PTwH buffer containing 3% (vol/vol) donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.4 Wash with PTwH buffer, changing the buffer every 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
3.1 Dehydration with 20% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Dehydration with 40% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Dehydration with 60% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Dehydration with 80% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Dehydration with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.6 Dehydration with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.7 Delipidation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM and 33% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.8 Delipidation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
3.9 RI matching with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI = 1.56) without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

4 Storage and Pre-imaging
4.1 Storage of the cleared tissue in 100% (vol/vol) DBE in a dark, airtight glass vial to prevent oxidation and fluorescence quenching. (Temperature: RT, Time: Long-term)
4.2 Pre-imaging preparation by mounting the tissue in a sealed imaging chamber completely filled with fresh DBE to ensure stable RI matching and prevent evaporation during 3D imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** TDE
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry]
**Justification:** TDE (2,2'-thiodiethanol) is a highly effective, water-soluble clearing agent perfectly suited for small intact organisms like *C. elegans*. It rapidly penetrates the cuticle without requiring harsh permeabilization steps that could compromise the delicate morphology of the 1 mm body. Most importantly, TDE exceptionally preserves the endogenous fluorescence of EGFP and mCherry, which is the primary requirement for tracing the nerve ring and pan-neuronal network without additional antibody staining. The graded TDE series simultaneously clears the tissue and smoothly adjusts the refractive index to ~1.52, matching glass and immersion oil for optimal high-resolution 3D imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Washing
1.1 Incubation with 1x PBS to remove residual fixative.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
1.2 Incubation with fresh 1x PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
2 Tissue Optical Clearing and Refractive Index Matching
2.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) TDE (2,2'-thiodiethanol) in 1x PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with 25% (vol/vol) TDE in 1x PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) TDE in 1x PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with 97% (vol/vol) TDE in distilled water (RI = 1.52).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3 Mounting and Pre-imaging Processing
3.1 Mounting the cleared C. elegans in fresh 97% TDE on a glass slide with a coverslip, sealed with an appropriate sealant.(Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)
3.2 Storage of the mounted slides in a dark environment to prevent photobleaching prior to imaging.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Until imaging)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** TDE
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry, DAPI]
**Justification:** TDE (2,2'-thiodiethanol) is a water-soluble clearing agent highly optimized for small organisms like *C. elegans*. It rapidly penetrates the nematode's tissues, provides excellent refractive index matching (up to ~1.515) for high-resolution 3D imaging of dense structures like the nerve ring, and perfectly preserves the endogenous fluorescence of both EGFP and mCherry without quenching. DAPI is included as an auxiliary nuclear counterstain to provide anatomical landmarks for the head ganglia and ventral nerve cord.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Washing and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) to wash post-fixed worms and permeabilize the cuticle. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

2 Auxiliary Nuclear Staining
2.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 μg/mL) in PBST to stain nuclei. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with PBS to wash out excess DAPI dye. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

3 Optical Clearing and Refractive Index Matching
3.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) TDE (2,2'-thiodiethanol) in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
3.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) TDE in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) TDE in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
3.4 Incubation with 97% (vol/vol) TDE in PBS (RI = 1.515). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Preservation and Pre-imaging Preparation
4.1 Mount the cleared C. elegans on a glass slide in a drop of fresh 97% TDE, using spacer beads (e.g., 50 μm) to prevent tissue crushing, and seal with a coverslip. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry, DAPI]
**Justification:** Ce3D (Clearing-enhanced 3D) is an aqueous clearing method specifically optimized for small biological samples like *C. elegans*. It provides excellent transparency while perfectly preserving endogenous fluorescent proteins (EGFP and mCherry) without the quenching often seen in solvent-based methods. The addition of DAPI provides a reliable nuclear reference channel, which is crucial for identifying stereotyped neuronal positions in *C. elegans* without interfering with the endogenous neural tracing signals.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pre-treatment and Staining
1.1 Wash the fixed C. elegans samples with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) to permeabilize the cuticle. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
1.2 Repeat the wash with fresh PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
1.3 Incubation with DAPI (1 μg/mL) in PBST for nuclear counterstaining. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
1.4 Wash with PBST to remove excess DAPI. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
1.5 Repeat the wash with fresh PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

2 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D clearing solution (86% wt/vol Histodenz, 1% vol/vol Triton X-100, 1% wt/vol thiourea, 20% vol/vol N-methylacetamide in PBS, RI = 1.50) in a microcentrifuge tube with gentle rotation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Preservation and Pre-imaging Preparation
3.1 Transfer the cleared C. elegans into a fresh drop of Ce3D solution on a glass slide. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes)
3.2 Place a coverslip over the sample, using spacer beads or double-sided tape to prevent crushing the 50–100 μm thick worms, and seal the edges with clear nail polish. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)
3.3 Store the mounted samples in the dark to allow complete stabilization before imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2.2 Incubation with 25% (vol/vol) TDE in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)
2.3 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) TDE in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
2.4 Incubation with 97% (vol/vol) TDE in PBS (RI ~ 1.52) for final clearing and RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** TDE
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin, Myosin VIIa + Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** TDE (2,2'-thiodiethanol) is a water-soluble clearing agent that is exceptionally gentle on delicate samples like 5 dpf zebrafish larvae. Unlike solvent-based methods which severely quench Phalloidin and cause tissue shrinkage, TDE perfectly preserves F-actin/stereocilia structures labeled by Phalloidin and maintains robust fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes. It provides rapid, seamless refractive index matching (up to RI ~1.51) without requiring harsh delipidation, making it ideal for high-resolution imaging of the superficial lateral line sensory epithelium.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Tissue Permeabilization and Blocking
1.1 Wash the fixed zebrafish larvae with PBS to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
1.2 Incubation with permeabilization solution containing 1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.3 Incubation with blocking buffer containing 5% (vol/vol) Normal Goat Serum and 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Fluorescent Labeling
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody against Myosin VIIa diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Wash with PBST (0.1% vol/vol Triton X-100 in PBS) for 4 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)
2.3 Incubation with Alexa Fluor secondary antibody and fluorescent Phalloidin diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.4 Wash with PBST (0.1% vol/vol Triton X-100 in PBS) for 4 times, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)

3 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) TDE in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) TDE in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) TDE in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) TDE in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Incubation with 97% (vol/vol) TDE in PBS (RI = 1.51). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

4 Storage and Pre-imaging Treatment
4.1 Mount the cleared zebrafish larvae in fresh 97% (vol/vol) TDE on a glass slide or imaging chamber. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
4.2 Store the mounted samples in 97% (vol/vol) TDE, protected from light, until imaging. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Long-term)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** TDE
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin, Tuj1 + Alexa Fluor, DAPI]
**Justification:** TDE (2,2'-thiodiethanol) is a highly water-soluble, aqueous clearing agent that rapidly clears small samples like 5 dpf zebrafish larvae while exceptionally preserving the fluorescence of chemical dyes and proteins. Unlike solvent-based methods that dehydrate tissue and destroy delicate F-actin structures, TDE perfectly preserves Phalloidin-labeled stereocilia bundles and antibody-labeled lateral line nerves (Tuj1), making it the ideal choice for high-resolution 3D imaging of the neuromast microenvironment.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Washing and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash with PBST (PBS containing 0.1% vol/vol Triton X-100). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes, change buffer every 10 minutes)
1.2 Incubation with permeabilization solution (PBS containing 1% vol/vol Triton X-100). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.3 Incubation with blocking buffer (PBS containing 0.1% vol/vol Triton X-100, 5% wt/vol Normal Goat Serum, 1% wt/vol BSA). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Fluorescent Labeling
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody against Tuj1 (1:500 dilution in blocking buffer) to label lateral line nerve fibers. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.2 Wash with PBST (PBS containing 0.1% vol/vol Triton X-100). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, change buffer every 30 minutes)
2.3 Incubation with Alexa Fluor secondary antibody (1:500 dilution), fluorescently conjugated Phalloidin (1:100 dilution) to label hair cell F-actin, and DAPI (5 µg/mL) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.4 Wash with PBST (PBS containing 0.1% vol/vol Triton X-100). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, change buffer every 30 minutes)

3 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) TDE (2,2'-thiodiethanol) in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) TDE in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) TDE in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) TDE in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Incubation with 97% (vol/vol) TDE in PBS (RI = 1.52) for final clearing and refractive index matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

4 Storage and Pre-imaging Preparation
4.1 Mount the cleared zebrafish larvae in fresh 97% (vol/vol) TDE on a glass slide with spacers or in an imaging chamber suitable for confocal/light-sheet microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)
4.2 Store the mounted samples in the dark until imaging. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Long-term)

**Chosen Method:** SeeDB2
**Chosen Labeling:** [Myosin VIIa + Alexa Fluor, Phalloidin, DAPI]
**Justification:** SeeDB2 is an aqueous clearing method utilizing iohexol (Omnipaque), which is specifically optimized for high-resolution imaging and the strict preservation of delicate F-actin structures (like stereocilia bundles) labeled by Phalloidin. Unlike ScaleS, which uses urea/sorbitol and can cause severe osmotic shock and tissue expansion if not carefully graded, SeeDB2 maintains constant tissue volume and prevents morphological deformation. The graded SeeDB2G series ensures gentle osmotic transitions for the fragile 5 dpf zebrafish. Myosin VIIa is a highly specific and robust identity marker for lateral line hair cells, while Phalloidin directly visualizes the apical F-actin bundles. Alexa Fluor and DAPI provide stable, multiplexed fluorescence compatible with the SeeDB2 chemical environment.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Permeabilization and Blocking
1.1 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS to permeabilize the intact larva.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.2 Incubation with blocking buffer containing 5% (vol/vol) Normal Goat Serum in 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Fluorescent Labeling
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody against Myosin VIIa diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Wash with 0.1% PBST, replacing the buffer every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
2.3 Incubation with Alexa Fluor-conjugated secondary antibody, fluorophore-conjugated Phalloidin, and DAPI diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.4 Wash with 0.1% PBST, replacing the buffer every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

3 Tissue Optical Clearing
3.1 Incubation with 25% (vol/vol) SeeDB2G (iohexol-based clearing solution) diluted in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) SeeDB2G diluted in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
3.3 Incubation with 75% (vol/vol) SeeDB2G diluted in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
3.4 Incubation with 100% SeeDB2G (RI = 1.52) with gentle rotation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

4 Refractive Index Matching and Imaging Preparation
4.1 Incubation with fresh 100% SeeDB2G for final refractive index matching and storage.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
4.2 Mount the cleared larva in fresh 100% SeeDB2G within a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber for 3D imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1 Washing
1.1 Incubation with 1x PBS to remove residual fixative.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
1.2 Incubation with fresh 1x PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

2.2 Incubation with fresh ClearSee solution to ensure complete chlorophyll removal and tissue clearing.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days)

3 Cell Wall Staining
3.1 Incubation with 0.1% (v/v) SCRI Renaissance 2200 diluted in ClearSee solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)

4 Destaining and Final RI Matching
4.1 Incubation with fresh ClearSee solution to wash out excess SCRI Renaissance 2200 dye.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day)

**Chosen Method:** ClearSee
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, YFP, SCRI Renaissance 2200]
**Justification:** ClearSee is specifically designed for plant tissue clearing. It excellently preserves endogenous GFP/YFP fluorescence while effectively clearing tissues and removing chlorophyll. The previous failure was likely due to insufficient incubation time and lack of vacuum infiltration for a 15-20 mm intact seedling. By extending the clearing time to 7 days with regular solution changes and adding a vacuum infiltration step, chlorophyll extraction and RI matching (RI=1.41) will be significantly improved. ClearSee is also highly compatible with the cell wall dye SCRI Renaissance 2200, allowing simultaneous deep imaging of reporter signals and cellular architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Tissue Washing
1.1 Incubation with 1x PBS to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
1.2 Incubation with fresh 1x PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

2 Tissue Optical Clearing and Chlorophyll Removal
2.1 Incubation with ClearSee solution (10% w/v xylitol, 15% w/v sodium deoxycholate, 25% w/v urea in water) under vacuum infiltration to enhance tissue penetration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with ClearSee solution with gentle shaking in the dark. Change with fresh ClearSee solution every 2 days until the tissue is completely transparent and chlorophyll is removed. (Temperature: RT, Time: 7 days)

3 Cell Wall Staining
3.1 Incubation with SCRI Renaissance 2200 diluted 1:1000 in ClearSee solution with gentle shaking in the dark. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 days)

4 Washing and Refractive Index Matching
4.1 Incubation with fresh ClearSee solution to wash out excess unbound dye. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day)
4.2 Incubation with fresh ClearSee solution for final refractive index matching (RI = 1.41) prior to imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous clearing method highly effective for dense, highly cellular tissues like skeletal muscle. It provides excellent transparency while avoiding the severe shrinkage and wrinkling typically caused by solvent-based methods, thereby preserving the delicate morphology and spatial distribution of the neuromuscular junction (NMJ). Alpha-bungarotoxin directly and specifically binds to acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) on the postsynaptic membrane, while PGP9.5 effectively labels the motor nerve terminals and axonal skeleton, allowing for comprehensive 3D spatial analysis of the NMJ structure at the whole-muscle scale.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Delipidation and Decolorization
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-L (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100 in dH2O) diluted in dH2O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-L with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
1.3 Incubation with fresh 100% CUBIC-L with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)

2 Washing
2.1 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.2 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Permeabilization and Blocking
3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

4 Fluorescent Labeling
4.1 Incubation with primary antibody (anti-PGP9.5, 1:200) and alpha-bungarotoxin conjugated with Alexa Fluor (1:500) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
4.2 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
4.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
4.4 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
4.5 Incubation with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor, 1:200) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
4.6 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
4.7 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
4.8 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

5 Post-fixation
5.1 Incubation with 1% PFA in PBS to stabilize the bound bungarotoxin and antibodies. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching
6.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 0.5 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine in dH2O, RI = 1.52) diluted in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6.3 Incubation with fresh 100% CUBIC-R+ with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

7.1 Store the sample in 100% CUBIC-R+ in a dark, airtight container. (Temperature: RT, Time: Long-term)
7.2 Mount the sample immersed in 100% CUBIC-R+ for light-sheet or confocal microscopy imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: During imaging)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** CUBIC
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin+Alexa Fluor, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)+Alexa Fluor, Phalloidin+Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** CUBIC is an excellent aqueous clearing method for intact, dense skeletal muscle (8 mm × 5 mm × 3 mm). It provides high transparency through efficient delipidation (CUBIC-L) and refractive index matching (CUBIC-R+) while maintaining a hydrated environment. This is critical because solvent-based clearing methods typically destroy Phalloidin (F-actin) binding and can severely quench alpha-bungarotoxin (AChR) fluorescence. CUBIC preserves these delicate probes and allows deep penetration of antibodies (TUJ1 for motor axons), perfectly supporting the 3D spatial mapping of NMJs, nerve terminals, and muscle fibers.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Delipidation and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash with PBS to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.2 Incubation with CUBIC-L solution (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100 in dH2O) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.3 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L solution with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.4 Wash with PBS to remove CUBIC-L. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2 Staining and Labeling
2.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) with multiple changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor), alpha-bungarotoxin (Alexa Fluor conjugated), and Phalloidin (Alexa Fluor conjugated) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.5 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) with multiple changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Refractive Index Matching and Pre-imaging
3.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ solution (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 0.5 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine) diluted in dH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-R+ solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.3 Incubation with fresh 100% CUBIC-R+ solution for final clearing and storage prior to imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin+Alexa Fluor, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)+Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** The previous THF/DBE solvent-based method causes severe dehydration, leading to significant muscle shrinkage and the quenching of peptide-based probes like alpha-bungarotoxin. CUBIC is an aqueous clearing method that provides excellent transparency for large, highly scattering tissues like whole skeletal muscle (8 mm × 5 mm × 3 mm) while maintaining low morphological deformation. Performing CUBIC-L delipidation *prior* to labeling significantly enhances the penetration depth of antibodies and alpha-bungarotoxin into the thick tissue. Furthermore, the CUBIC-R matching solution highly preserves the fluorescence of Alexa Fluor conjugates, ensuring strong, stable signals for both the AChR (via alpha-bungarotoxin) and the axonal skeleton/motor nerve terminals (via β-III Tubulin) for high-resolution 3D imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Tissue Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L solution (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100 in dH2O) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
1.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L solution with gentle shaking to ensure complete delipidation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)

2 Washing
2.1 Wash with PBS to remove residual CUBIC-L. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.2 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Blocking and Permeabilization
3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% BSA, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

4 Immunostaining and Labeling
4.1 Incubation with primary antibody against β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
4.2 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
4.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
4.4 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
4.5 Incubation with Alexa Fluor-conjugated secondary antibody and Alexa Fluor-conjugated alpha-bungarotoxin diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
4.6 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) to remove unbound probes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
4.7 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
4.8 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

5 Refractive Index Matching
5.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R solution (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide in dH2O) diluted in dH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
5.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-R solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
5.3 Incubation with fresh 100% CUBIC-R solution until the muscle tissue becomes completely transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor, Phalloidin]
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous tissue clearing method highly suitable for whole organs like the mouse stomach. Crucially, unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO) that dehydrate tissue with methanol or THF and destroy F-actin, CUBIC preserves F-actin structures. This allows the prioritized use of Phalloidin to label the circular and longitudinal muscle layers as a structural reference. Simultaneously, PGP9.5 serves as a robust pan-neuronal marker to trace vagal nerve endings across the gastric layers. CUBIC provides excellent transparency and antibody penetration for a 20 mm × 15 mm × 8 mm sample.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Delipidation and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L solution (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100 in dH2O) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
1.2 Refresh with new CUBIC-L solution with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
1.3 Wash with PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.4 Wash with PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.5 Wash with PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Immunostaining and F-actin Labeling
2.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody (anti-PGP9.5) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days)
2.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.4 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.5 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2.8 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.9 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

请根据该科学问题自行选择合适的荧光/标记策略，并基于所选标记样本选择匹配的组织透明方法。若已有 EGFP 与 tdTomato 内源荧光报告信号可以直接完成投射神经元和轴突示踪，应优先保留该信号，不应额外选择抗体替代同一主示踪目标。请仅输出 protocol，第 1 行写明所选荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** FDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, tdTomato]
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method specifically optimized to preserve endogenous fluorescent proteins (like EGFP and tdTomato) while achieving the high transparency required for large tissue samples such as whole mouse brains. By utilizing low temperature (4 ℃) and alkaline pH (pH 9.0) during the dehydration process, it effectively prevents the fluorescence quenching typically associated with solvent clearing. This makes it ideal for tracing long-range neural circuits and fine axons across the whole brain without the need for additional antibody staining.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Dehydration
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) peroxide-free tetrahydrofuran (THF) in pH 9.0 adjusted distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) peroxide-free THF in pH 9.0 adjusted distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) peroxide-free THF in pH 9.0 adjusted distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) peroxide-free THF with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) peroxide-free THF with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) peroxide-free THF with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

2 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (RI = 1.56) with gentle shaking until the brain becomes completely transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Storage and Pre-imaging
3.1 Store the cleared brain submerged in 100% DBE in a dark, airtight glass vial to prevent oxidation and preserve endogenous fluorescence prior to light-sheet imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: Ongoing)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, tdTomato, MAP2+Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous tissue clearing method that excellently preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins (EGFP and tdTomato) while achieving high transparency for whole mouse brains. It is highly compatible with whole-mount immunostaining, allowing the addition of MAP2 to label dendritic structures. This combination perfectly addresses the need to trace endogenous long-range projections and visualize their spatial relationship with local neuronal structures in terminal-rich areas without quenching the endogenous tracers.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-L (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100 in dH2O) diluted in dH2O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-L with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, refresh buffer every 2 days)

2 Wash
2.1 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, refresh buffer 3 times)

3 Immunostaining
3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% BSA, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody (anti-MAP2) diluted in staining buffer (1% BSA, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)
3.3 Wash with washing buffer (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, refresh buffer 3 times)
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor) diluted in staining buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)
3.5 Wash with washing buffer (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, refresh buffer 3 times)

4 Post-fixation
4.1 Incubation with 1% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS to fix antibodies. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
4.2 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

5 Refractive Index Matching
5.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 0.5 vol% N-butyldiethanolamine in dH2O, RI = 1.52) diluted in dH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
5.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-R+ with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

6 Storage and Pre-imaging
6.1 Store the sample in 100% CUBIC-R+ in a dark container. (Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinitely)
6.2 Mount the sample in 100% CUBIC-R+ or a matched RI medium (RI = 1.52) for light-sheet or confocal imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: During imaging)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, tdTomato, MAP2+Alexa Fluor, DAPI]
**Justification:** CUBIC is highly effective for whole-mouse brain delipidation while exceptionally preserving endogenous fluorescent proteins (EGFP and tdTomato). The previous SWITCH protocol failed because a 2-day SDS treatment without proper permeabilization is insufficient for intact whole-brain delipidation and deep antibody penetration. CUBIC-L provides thorough, gentle delipidation over several days, which is critical for clearing a 10 mm × 8 mm × 6 mm intact brain. MAP2 is selected as the ideal dendritic cytoskeleton marker, paired with a far-red Alexa Fluor to avoid spectral overlap with endogenous EGFP/tdTomato signals. Finally, CUBIC-R+ provides uniform refractive index matching (RI ~1.52) for high-resolution 3D imaging without quenching the preserved signals.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L solution (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100 in dH2O) with gentle shaking for 3 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
1.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L solution with gentle shaking for 3 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)

2 Wash
2.1 Wash with PBS with gentle shaking for 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
2.2 Wash with PBS with gentle shaking for 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBS with gentle shaking for 16 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 16 hours)

3 Immunolabeling
3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% BSA, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody (anti-MAP2) diluted in blocking buffer for 5 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 120 hours)
3.3 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
3.4 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
3.5 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 16 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 16 hours)
3.6 Incubation with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor) and nuclear stain (DAPI) diluted in blocking buffer for 5 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 120 hours)
3.7 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
3.8 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
3.9 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 16 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 16 hours)

4 Post-fixation
4.1 Incubation with 1% PFA in PBS to fix bound antibodies for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
4.2 Wash with PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching
5.1 Incubation with 50% CUBIC-R+ solution (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 0.5 vol% N-butyldiethanolamine in dH2O) diluted in dH2O for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
5.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-R+ solution for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
5.3 Incubation with fresh 100% CUBIC-R+ solution for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [C-FoS+Alexa Fluor, PI]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly effective for clearing both lipid-rich whole brain tissue and dense, collagen-rich muscular tissue like the tongue. It is the established gold standard for whole-organ immunolabeling of immediate early genes (IEGs) such as C-FoS to map neural activation. PI is selected as the auxiliary channel because standard iDISCO+ utilizes methanol dehydration which degrades F-actin (making Phalloidin unsuitable); however, PI provides excellent nuclear contrast that is fully sufficient for the anatomical registration of tongue muscle fibers and brain regions.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pre-treatment
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.7 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM (dichloromethane) and 33% (vol/vol) methanol for delipidation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.8 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol to wash out DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.9 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.10 Incubation with chilled 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes methanol) for bleaching. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

2 Rehydration and Permeabilization
2.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.5 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.6 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.7 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.8 Incubation with permeabilization solution (PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 20% DMSO, and 0.3 M glycine). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

3 Immunolabeling
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution (PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, and 6% Donkey Serum). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody C-FoS (1:500) in PTwH buffer (PBS containing 0.2% Tween-20, 10 mg/ml heparin, 5% DMSO, and 3% Donkey Serum). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
3.3 Wash with PTwH buffer (PBS containing 0.2% Tween-20 and 10 mg/ml heparin), changing buffer every 4-5 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor (1:500) and PI (10 ug/ml) in PTwH buffer (PBS containing 0.2% Tween-20, 10 mg/ml heparin, and 3% Donkey Serum). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
3.5 Wash with PTwH buffer, changing buffer every 4-5 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.7 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM and 33% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
4.8 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM to wash out methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
4.9 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
4.10 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Di-benzyl ether, RI = 1.56) for refractive index matching and storage. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Labeling:** [C-FoS+Alexa Fluor, Npas4 (IEGs)+Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous clearing method that completely avoids methanol and DBE, directly solving the user's issues of severe tissue shrinkage, antigenicity loss, and fluorescence quenching caused by harsh organic solvents. The corrected protocol incorporates CUBIC-L for thorough delipidation and permeabilization, extended blocking and antibody incubation times (7 days) for deep whole-tissue penetration, multiple washing steps to reduce background, and a gentle RI matching process (CUBIC-R+) to perfectly preserve the dual IEG (C-FoS and Npas4) fluorescent signals for whole-brain 3D imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Delipidation and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-L (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100 in dH2O) diluted in dH2O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-L with gentle shaking, refreshing the solution every 2 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)

2 Washing
2.1 Wash with PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.2 Wash with PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Blocking
3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (PBS containing 5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100, and 1% BSA). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

4 Primary Antibody Incubation
4.1 Incubation with primary antibodies (anti-C-FoS and anti-Npas4) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)

5 Washing
5.1 Wash with PBST (PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
5.2 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
5.3 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
5.4 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6 Secondary Antibody Incubation
6.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor conjugated) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)

7 Washing
7.1 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
7.2 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
7.3 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
7.4 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

8 Post-fixation
8.1 Incubation with 1% PFA in PBS to crosslink bound antibodies and preserve fluorescence. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
8.2 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** SeeDB2
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]
**Justification:** SeeDB2 is an aqueous tissue clearing method that utilizes Omnipaque 350 (iohexol) for refractive index matching without the use of organic solvents or strong lipid-extracting detergents. Because the scientific goal requires tracing sensory nerve projections using lipophilic dyes (DiI and DiD), solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO) or strong detergent-based methods (e.g., standard CUBIC) cannot be used as they will extract membrane lipids and completely wash out the tracer signals. SeeDB2 perfectly preserves lipid-bound DiI and DiD signals while providing high transparency (RI = 1.52), enabling high-resolution 3D mapping of the intact spinal cord, thalamus, and somatosensory cortex.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
1.1 Wash the fixed tissues (intact spinal cord, thalamus, somatosensory cortex) with PBS to remove excess fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 2% (wt/vol) saponin in PBS to mildly permeabilize the tissue without extracting lipophilic dyes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
1.3 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) SeeDB2G solution (Omnipaque 350) in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
1.4 Incubation with 75% (vol/vol) SeeDB2G solution (Omnipaque 350) in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) SeeDB2G solution (Omnipaque 350, RI = 1.52) with gentle rotation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) SeeDB2G solution (Omnipaque 350, RI = 1.52) with gentle rotation to ensure complete clearing of the 3 cm spinal cord and brain regions. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

2 Storage and Pre-imaging Preparation
2.1 Store the cleared samples in 100% SeeDB2G solution in the dark to prevent photobleaching of DiI and DiD. (Temperature: RT, Time: Long-term)
2.2 Mount the samples in 100% SeeDB2G solution within a glass-bottom imaging chamber suitable for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** SeeDB2
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiO, DAPI]
**Justification:** Lipophilic tracer dyes (DiI, DiO) are highly susceptible to extraction by organic solvents and strong detergents used in many clearing protocols. SeeDB2 is an aqueous, detergent-free clearing method based on iohexol (Omnipaque) that perfectly preserves lipophilic dyes, endogenous fluorescence, and fine tissue morphology without lipid extraction. DAPI is included as an auxiliary nuclear marker for structural registration, perfectly matching the requirement to avoid unnecessary neural antibodies.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Auxiliary Staining
1.1 Incubation with DAPI (5 µg/mL in PBS) to provide auxiliary nuclear contrast for structural registration (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
1.2 Wash with PBS to remove excess DAPI (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

2 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
2.1 Incubation with 33% (vol/vol) SeeDB2G (33% Omnipaque 350, 5% glycerol in PBS) with gentle shaking (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) SeeDB2G (50% Omnipaque 350, 5% glycerol in PBS) with gentle shaking (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.3 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) SeeDB2G (66% Omnipaque 350, 5% glycerol in PBS) with gentle shaking (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) SeeDB2G (Omnipaque 350 containing 5% glycerol, RI = 1.46) with gentle shaking (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

3 Storage and Pre-imaging Processing
3.1 Storage in fresh 100% (vol/vol) SeeDB2G protected from light (Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinitely)
3.2 Mounting in 100% (vol/vol) SeeDB2G within an imaging chamber suitable for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** TDE
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]
**Justification:** The previous SDS-based clearing and glycerol matching failed because SDS is a strong detergent that extracts tissue lipids, thereby washing out lipophilic tracer dyes like DiI and DiD. TDE (2,2'-thiodiethanol) is an aqueous clearing agent that does not require delipidation, thus perfectly preserving lipid-bound DiI and DiD signals. It provides a high refractive index (up to ~1.52 at 97%) for excellent and uniform transparency in large brain and spinal cord tissues without the need for organic solvents or detergents.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Tissue Washing
1.1 Incubation with 1x PBS to remove excess fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
1.2 Incubation with fresh 1x PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

2 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) TDE (2,2'-thiodiethanol) in 1x PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) TDE in 1x PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) TDE in 1x PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) TDE in 1x PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.5 Incubation with 97% (vol/vol) TDE in 1x PBS (RI ~ 1.52) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.6 Incubation with fresh 97% (vol/vol) TDE in 1x PBS for final RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Storage and Pre-imaging Preparation
3.1 Mount the cleared spinal cord, thalamus, and somatosensory cortex tissues in fresh 97% (vol/vol) TDE within a suitable imaging chamber to maintain RI matching during 3D imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor, DAPI]
**Justification:** PEGASOS is highly optimized for hard tissues like bone, featuring a dedicated EDTA decalcification step and a Quadrol decolorization step that effectively removes heme from the bone marrow. This allows deep penetration of antibodies into the dense mineralized matrix and marrow cavity without destroying the tissue architecture. β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) serves as a robust pan-neuronal marker to trace the fine nerve fibers connecting the CNS and PNS through the skull and long bones, while DAPI provides essential structural context by labeling nuclei.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Decalcification
1.1 Incubation with 20% (wt/vol) EDTA aqueous solution (pH 7.4) with daily changes to soften the mineralized bone matrix. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)

2 Decolorization
2.1 Incubation with 25% (vol/vol) Quadrol aqueous solution to remove endogenous heme from the bone marrow. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)

3 Permeabilization and Blocking
3.1 Wash with PBS to remove excess Quadrol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
3.2 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.3 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4 Immunolabeling
4.1 Incubation with primary antibody anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) (1:200 dilution) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)
4.2 Wash with washing buffer (0.1% Tween-20 in PBS) changing buffer every 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
4.3 Incubation with secondary antibody conjugated with Alexa Fluor (1:500 dilution) and DAPI (1:1000 dilution) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)
4.4 Wash with washing buffer (0.1% Tween-20 in PBS) changing buffer every 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

5 Delipidation and Dehydration
5.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) tert-butanol (tB-OH) aqueous solution containing 3% (wt/vol) Quadrol. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
5.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) tert-butanol (tB-OH) aqueous solution containing 3% (wt/vol) Quadrol. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
5.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) tert-butanol (tB-OH) aqueous solution containing 3% (wt/vol) Quadrol. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
5.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert-butanol (tB-OH). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
5.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) tert-butanol (tB-OH). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

6 Clearing, Refractive Index Matching and Preservation
6.1 Incubation with PEGASOS clearing medium (75% vol/vol benzyl benzoate, 25% vol/vol PEG-500 methyl ether, and 3% wt/vol Quadrol, RI = 1.54). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
6.2 Incubation with fresh PEGASOS clearing medium for final RI matching and storage before imaging. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP+Alexa Fluor, PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor, DAPI]
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for highly mineralized bone tissues (like skull and femur) and lipid-rich bone marrow. It utilizes EDTA for gentle decalcification while preserving endogenous structures, meningeal connections, and antigenicity. PGP9.5 serves as an excellent pan-neural marker from the provided list, while CGRP specifically identifies the sensory nerve fibers required by the scientific goal. Alexa Fluor dyes provide robust fluorescence in the DBE clearing solvent, and DAPI serves as an auxiliary nuclear counterstain to outline bone marrow cavities, bone pores, and sutures.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Decalcification
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA aqueous solution (pH 7.4) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 14 days, change solution every 2 days)
1.2 Wash with 1x PBS to remove excess EDTA. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, change buffer 3 times)

2 Permeabilization and Blocking
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.5% vol/vol Triton X-100 in 1x PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% wt/vol BSA, 0.5% vol/vol Triton X-100 in 1x PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Immunolabeling
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies (anti-CGRP and anti-PGP9.5) diluted in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days)
3.2 Wash with washing buffer (0.1% vol/vol Triton X-100 in 1x PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, change buffer every 8 hours)
3.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor conjugated) and DAPI diluted in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days)
3.4 Wash with washing buffer (0.1% vol/vol Triton X-100 in 1x PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, change buffer every 8 hours)

4 Dehydration
4.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) Tetrahydrofuran (THF) in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
4.2 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) THF in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
4.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) THF in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
4.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
4.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) THF. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

5 Clearing and RI Matching
5.1 Incubation with 100% Dichloromethane (DCM) for delipidation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI = 1.56). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6 Storage and Pre-imaging
6.1 Store the cleared samples in 100% DBE in a dark, airtight container. (Temperature: RT, Time: Long-term)
6.2 Mount the sample in a quartz cuvette or imaging chamber filled with fresh DBE prior to 3D light-sheet or confocal imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** BoneClear
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor, IB4 (凝集素) + Alexa Fluor, DAPI]
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for intact bone, bone marrow, and adjacent tissues (like meninges). It incorporates a gentle EDTA decalcification step that preserves tissue architecture and is highly compatible with whole-mount immunostaining. Using β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) reliably identifies pan-nerve fibers, while IB4 effectively labels the vascular lumen as an auxiliary channel. The THF/DCM/DBE solvent system provides excellent refractive index matching and transparency for dense, calcified tissues, enabling high-resolution 3D mapping of the CNS-PNS connections through bone channels.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Decalcification
1.1 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA aqueous solution (pH 7.4) with gentle shaking for decalcification. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 10 days)
1.2 Wash with 1x PBS to remove excess EDTA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Permeabilization and Blocking
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% vol/vol Triton X-100, 20% vol/vol DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in 1x PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution (0.2% vol/vol Triton X-100, 10% vol/vol DMSO, 6% vol/vol donkey serum in 1x PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

3 Immunostaining and Labeling
3.1 Incubation with primary antibody β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) and IB4 (凝集素) in antibody dilution buffer (0.2% vol/vol Tween-20, 10 μg/mL heparin, 5% vol/vol DMSO, 3% vol/vol donkey serum in 1x PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days)
3.2 Wash with PTwH buffer (0.2% vol/vol Tween-20, 10 μg/mL heparin in 1x PBS) for 5 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)
3.3 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor and DAPI in antibody dilution buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days)
3.4 Wash with PTwH buffer for 5 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)

4 Dehydration
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) Tetrahydrofuran (THF) aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) Tetrahydrofuran (THF) aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) Tetrahydrofuran (THF) aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) Tetrahydrofuran (THF) aqueous solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Tetrahydrofuran (THF). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
4.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Tetrahydrofuran (THF). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

5 Delipidation and Refractive Index Matching
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) for delipidation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI = 1.56) for refractive index matching and clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6 Storage and Pre-imaging
6.1 Store the cleared samples in 100% (vol/vol) DBE in a dark environment. (Temperature: RT, Time: Long-term)
6.2 Mount the sample in 100% (vol/vol) DBE in a sealed, solvent-resistant imaging chamber prior to light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

我需要对小鼠颅骨、股骨、骨髓和脑膜进行透明化处理，用于研究 CNS 与 PNS 通过骨组织的解剖连接。样本包括约 1.5 cm × 1 cm × 0.5 mm 的颅骨、约 1.5 cm 长的股骨，以及骨髓和脑膜结构，已完成固定和后固定。科学目标是同时标记骨组织中的 CGRP 阳性感觉神经纤维和泛神经纤维网络，或者在解剖连接分析中显示骨内/脑膜泛神经纤维和较粗大轴突结构，比较神经纤维在骨缝、骨孔、骨髓腔、脑膜界面和长骨内部的空间分布。

我在进行小鼠颅骨透明化实验时遇到问题：按照标准 BoneClear protocol 操作，固定后进行甲醇梯度脱水和 bleaching，然后进行远红荧光二抗孵育和 RI matching。结果骨组织仍然不透明，无法观察骨内结构，且远红信号很弱。该流程可能缺少充分脱钙、骨基质软化、深层透化和长时间抗体渗透，也可能因 bleaching 或脱水步骤过强导致抗原和荧光信号受损。请根据上述科学目标，在不引入给定标记物列表之外靶点或表外荧光团的前提下，重新选择或调整荧光/标记策略与组织透明方法。修正版应适合矿化骨组织脱钙、骨髓和脑膜结构保留、神经纤维双信号检测、低背景、深层抗体渗透和三维成像。

请仅输出修正后的 protocol，第 1 行写明应保留或更换的荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, MBP + Alexa Fluor 647]
**Justification:** CUBIC (specifically the CUBIC-B variant optimized for bone) utilizes EDTA and imidazole for simultaneous decalcification and delipidation, effectively softening the mineralized bone matrix without the harsh methanol dehydration or H2O2 bleaching that damages antigens and fluorophores in standard BoneClear. The aqueous nature of CUBIC preserves fragile endogenous structures like bone marrow and meninges better than organic solvents, while allowing deep antibody penetration for pan-nerve (PGP9.5) and large myelinated axon (MBP) visualization with high signal-to-noise ratio.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Decalcification and Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC-B solution (10% w/v EDTA, 15% w/v imidazole, 15% w/v Triton X-100 in dH2O) with gentle shaking to decalcify and delipidate the bone tissue. Refresh solution every 2 days.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)

2 Washing
2.1 Incubation with PBS to remove CUBIC-B reagents. Refresh solution 3 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Permeabilization and Blocking
3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% w/v BSA, 0.5% v/v Triton X-100, 0.05% w/v sodium azide in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

4 Primary Antibody Incubation
4.1 Incubation with primary antibodies (anti-PGP9.5 and anti-MBP) diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)

5 Washing
5.1 Incubation with PBST (0.1% v/v Triton X-100 in PBS). Refresh solution daily.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days)

6 Secondary Antibody Incubation
6.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647) diluted in blocking buffer. Protect from light.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)

7 Washing
7.1 Incubation with PBST (0.1% v/v Triton X-100 in PBS). Refresh solution daily. Protect from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days)

8 Post-fixation
8.1 Incubation with 1% (w/v) PFA in PBS to crosslink antibodies and preserve fluorescence during RI matching.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
8.2 Incubation with PBS to wash out residual PFA.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

9 Refractive Index (RI) Matching
9.1 Incubation with 50% (v/v) CUBIC-R+ solution (45% w/v antipyrine, 30% w/v nicotinamide, 0.5% v/v N-butyldiethanolamine in dH2O, RI = 1.52) diluted in dH2O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
9.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-R+ solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
9.3 Incubation with fresh 100% CUBIC-R+ solution until the bone tissue becomes completely transparent.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (酪氨酸羟化酶) + Alexa Fluor, VIP + Alexa Fluor, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor, DAPI]
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard, calcified tissues like the femur, tibia, and skull. It incorporates an extended EDTA decalcification step to soften the bone matrix, followed by solvent-based dehydration and delipidation (THF/DCM/DBE) to effectively clear the highly lipid-rich bone marrow cavity while preserving the structural integrity of the endosteum. TH and VIP specifically identify noradrenergic and peptidergic sympathetic nerves, respectively. CD31 and DAPI provide the necessary spatial reference for the perivascular and hematopoietic niches without substituting the primary neural targets.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Decalcification
1.1 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA (pH 7.4) aqueous solution with daily buffer changes to decalcify the hard bone tissue. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 14 days)
1.2 Wash with 1x PBS to remove excess EDTA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

2 Permeabilization and Blocking
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% vol/vol Triton X-100, 20% vol/vol DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in 1x PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution (0.2% vol/vol Triton X-100, 10% vol/vol DMSO, 6% vol/vol donkey serum in 1x PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

3 Immunolabeling
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies (anti-TH, anti-VIP, anti-CD31, 1:200 dilution) diluted in washing buffer (0.2% vol/vol Tween-20, 10 μg/mL heparin, 5% vol/vol DMSO, 3% vol/vol donkey serum in 1x PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days)
3.2 Wash with washing buffer (0.2% vol/vol Tween-20, 10 μg/mL heparin in 1x PBS) with buffer changes every 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor conjugated, 1:400 dilution) and DAPI (1 μg/mL) diluted in washing buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days)
3.4 Wash with washing buffer (0.2% vol/vol Tween-20, 10 μg/mL heparin in 1x PBS) with buffer changes every 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4 Dehydration
4.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) Tetrahydrofuran (THF) in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
4.2 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) THF in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
4.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) THF in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
4.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
4.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) THF. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

5 Delipidation and Refractive Index Matching
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) for delipidation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI = 1.56) for refractive index matching and optical clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6 Storage and Pre-imaging
6.1 Store the cleared bone samples in fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in dark glass vials to prevent fluorescence quenching and maintain transparency prior to light-sheet imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: Long-term)
