model_response:
**Chosen Method:** CUBIC
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor, TH+Alexa Fluor, DAPI]
**Justification:** CUBIC is highly effective for decolorizing blood- and myoglobin-rich tissues like the whole heart because the aminoalcohols in CUBIC-L efficiently elute heme. It is an aqueous method that causes minimal tissue deformation, satisfying the low-deformation requirement. The inclusion of CUBIC-L for thorough delipidation and decolorization, followed by prolonged antibody incubation and sufficient washing, resolves the previous issues of opacity, red background, and weak signals. Since ChAT is restricted from the provided marker list, PGP9.5 is selected to comprehensively label the intrinsic cardiac ganglia (which are predominantly cholinergic), while TH specifically labels the noradrenergic sympathetic nerve fibers, achieving the dual-network mapping goal.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Delipidation and Decolorization
1.1 Wash the fixed heart with PBS to remove excess fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-L (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100 in distilled water) to initiate delipidation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.3 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-L with gentle shaking to elute heme/myoglobin and deeply delipidate. Refresh the solution every 2 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 days)
1.4 Wash with PBS to completely remove CUBIC-L. Refresh PBS 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2 Permeabilization and Blocking
2.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% BSA, 0.5% Triton X-100, 0.01% sodium azide in PBS) to prevent non-specific binding and enhance permeability. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)

3 Immunostaining
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies (anti-PGP9.5 and anti-TH) diluted in the blocking buffer with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
3.2 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) to remove unbound primary antibodies. Refresh buffer 4 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)
3.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor) and DAPI diluted in the blocking buffer with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
3.4 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) to remove unbound secondary antibodies and dyes. Refresh buffer 4 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)

4 Post-fixation
4.1 Incubation with 1% PFA in PBS to crosslink antibodies and preserve fluorescence during clearing. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
4.2 Wash with PBS to remove residual PFA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

5 Refractive Index Matching and Storage
5.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 5 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine in distilled water) to initiate RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
5.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-R+ with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)
5.3 Incubation with fresh 100% CUBIC-R+ for final optical clearing. The sample is now ready for 3D imaging and can be stored in this solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)

**Chosen Method:** MACS
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD3 + Alexa Fluor, CD8 + Alexa Fluor, DAPI]
**Justification:** MACS is an aqueous clearing method that perfectly preserves the structural integrity of fragile 500 μm deparaffinized sections without the shrinkage or morphological distortion associated with solvent-based methods. It offers excellent preservation of fluorescent signals, which is ideal for multiplexed imaging of the tumor microenvironment to distinguish pan-T (CD3) and cytotoxic T (CD8) cells. Since paraffin sections are already delipidated by xylene during standard processing, MACS provides a rapid, progressive refractive index (RI) matching process that achieves high transparency while maintaining intact tissue architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Immunofluorescence Labeling
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (PBS containing 5% normal goat serum and 0.3% Triton X-100) to block non-specific binding and permeabilize tissue. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies (anti-CD3 and anti-CD8) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (PBST) to remove unbound primary antibodies. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor) and DAPI diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.5 Wash with PBST to remove unbound secondary antibodies and dyes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.6 Wash with standard PBS to remove excess detergent prior to clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 solution (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in water, RI = 1.40). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 solution (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in water, RI = 1.48). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 solution (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in water, RI = 1.51). (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

3 Preservation and Pre-imaging Preparation
3.1 Mount the cleared section in fresh MACS-R2 solution on a glass slide using an imaging spacer (e.g., 500 μm depth) to prevent tissue compression and structural damage. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)
3.2 Seal the coverslip edges with curing silicone or clear nail polish to prevent evaporation of the clearing agent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
3.3 Store the mounted sample in the dark until 3D confocal or light-sheet imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: Until imaging)

1.3 Wash with 0.1 M PBS to remove CUBIC-L. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies against Nephrin (NPHS1) and Podocin (NPHS2) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.5 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3 Refractive Index Matching
3.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ solution (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 0.5 vol% N-butyldiethanolamine in dH2O) diluted in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-R+ solution (RI = 1.52) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4 Storage and Pre-imaging Treatment
4.1 Store the cleared sample in fresh 100% CUBIC-R+ solution in a dark container. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
4.2 Mount the sample in 100% CUBIC-R+ for high-resolution 3D imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor, HuC/D + Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** CUBIC is highly effective for clearing dense, lipid-rich clinical human brain tissues while minimizing structural degradation, thus preserving clinical tissue morphology. The CUBIC-L step provides efficient delipidation, and CUBIC-R+ achieves excellent refractive index matching (RI ~1.52) suitable for deep light-sheet microscopy. NeuN (RBFOX3) and HuC/D are robust, specific markers for mature neuron cell bodies and nuclei. Using Alexa Fluor dyes (e.g., Alexa Fluor 488 and 647) offers bright, photostable signals with distinct emission spectra to avoid cross-talk in dual-target imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Tissue Pre-treatment and Delipidation
1.1 Wash the fixed human brain tissue block with PBS to remove excess fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.2 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100 in water) for delipidation, replacing with fresh solution halfway. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days)
1.3 Wash with PBS with gentle shaking to remove CUBIC-L completely. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2 Immunolabeling
2.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies (anti-NeuN (RBFOX3) and anti-HuC/D) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
2.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) with gentle shaking, changing the buffer every 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies (conjugated with distinct Alexa Fluor dyes, e.g., Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
2.5 Wash with PBST with gentle shaking, changing the buffer every 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.6 Post-fixation with 1% PFA in PBS to crosslink antibodies and preserve fluorescence. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.7 Wash with PBS to remove residual PFA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Refractive Index (RI) Matching
3.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 0.5 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine in water) diluted in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-R+ solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

4 Storage and Pre-imaging Preparation
4.1 Store the cleared sample in fresh 100% CUBIC-R+ in the dark until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: > 24 hours)
4.2 Mount the sample in a light-sheet imaging chamber filled with 100% CUBIC-R+ (RI = 1.52) and allow it to equilibrate to ensure optical homogeneity before imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor, Lectin, DAPI]
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous clearing method that provides excellent transparency for lung tissue while preserving the delicate alveolar architecture much better than solvent-based methods, which often cause severe shrinkage and structural collapse. It is highly compatible with endogenous fluorescence, chemical dyes (DAPI), and whole-mount immunostaining (CD31 for endothelium). The functional perfused vascular lumen can be effectively labeled via *in vivo* intravenous injection of fluorescent Lectin prior to fixation, a signal which CUBIC retains perfectly.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Tissue Delipidation and Clearing
1.1 Wash the fixed 1.5 mm lung tissue block with PBS to remove excess fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-L (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100 in water) diluted in PBS. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)
1.3 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-L solution with gentle shaking to thoroughly delipidate the tissue. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
1.4 Wash with PBS with gentle shaking to completely remove CUBIC-L, changing the buffer 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2 Fluorescent Labeling
2.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody anti-CD31 (PECAM1) (1:100 dilution) in blocking buffer to label the vascular endothelium. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) with gentle shaking, changing the buffer 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
2.4 Incubation with Alexa Fluor-conjugated secondary antibody (1:200 dilution) and DAPI (5 µg/mL) in blocking buffer. (Note: The functional perfused lumen is assumed to be pre-labeled via in vivo intravenous injection of fluorescent Lectin prior to sacrifice). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.5 Wash with PBST with gentle shaking, changing the buffer 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

3 Refractive Index (RI) Matching
3.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 0.5% N-butyldiethanolamine in water, RI = 1.52) diluted in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-R+ solution with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4 Storage and Pre-imaging Treatment
4.1 Store the cleared and labeled sample in 100% CUBIC-R+ in the dark. (Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinitely)
4.2 Mount the sample in an imaging chamber filled with fresh 100% CUBIC-R+ (RI = 1.52) to prevent drying and maintain transparency for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS
**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC) + Alexa Fluor, F4/80 (小鼠) + Alexa Fluor, DAPI]

B220 (PTPRC) serves to label pan-immune/lymphocyte populations, and F4/80 specifically identifies the myeloid/macrophage subset. Alexa Fluor dyes and DAPI provide strong, stable signals for deep tissue light-sheet imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Decalcification
1.1 Incubation with 20% (wt/vol) EDTA aqueous solution (pH 7.4) with gentle shaking to remove bone mineralization. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
1.2 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Decolorization
2.1 Incubation with 25% (vol/vol) Quadrol in water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 day)
2.2 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Permeabilization and Blocking
3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (10% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 day)

4 Immunolabeling
4.1 Incubation with primary antibodies (anti-B220 (PTPRC) and anti-F4/80 (小鼠)) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
4.2 Wash with washing buffer (0.2% Tween-20, 10 µg/mL heparin in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day)
4.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor conjugated) and DAPI diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
4.4 Wash with washing buffer (0.2% Tween-20, 10 µg/mL heparin in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day)

5 Delipidation and Dehydration
5.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) tert-butanol (tB-OH) in water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
5.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) tB-OH in water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
5.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) tB-OH in water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
5.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tB-OH. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
5.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) tB-OH. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

6 Clearing and RI Matching
6.1 Incubation with PEGASOS clearing medium (BB-PEG: 75% vol/vol benzyl benzoate, 25% vol/vol PEG-500 methacrylate, 3% wt/vol Quadrol, RI = 1.54). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 day)

7 Storage and Pre-imaging
7.1 Store the cleared sample in PEGASOS clearing medium in a sealed container in the dark. (Temperature: RT, Time: Long-term)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin, Osx (Osterix) + Alexa Fluor, Osteocalcin + Alexa Fluor, DAPI]
**Justification:** CUBIC is a highly efficient aqueous clearing method that completely avoids harsh organic solvent dehydration, thereby perfectly preserving the pre-perfused Lectin vascular signal and endogenous fluorescence. By utilizing the CUBIC-B reagent (containing 10% EDTA), it achieves mild decalcification suitable for a 5 mm femur sample, preventing structural damage to the trabecular bone while allowing deep penetration of antibodies for distinguishing osteogenic lineage cells (Osx) and bone matrix proteins (Osteocalcin).

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Delipidation
1.1 Wash fixed bone samples with PBS to remove excess fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-L (10 wt% N-butyldiethanolamine, 10 wt% Triton X-100 in water) diluted in distilled water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)
1.3 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-L with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
1.4 Wash with PBS to remove CUBIC-L. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2 Mild Decalcification
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-B (10 wt% EDTA, 10 wt% Triton X-100, 10 wt% imidazole in water) with gentle shaking to mildly decalcify the bone matrix. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)
2.2 Wash with PBS to remove CUBIC-B. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3 Immunostaining
3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.2 Incubation with primary antibodies (anti-Osx and anti-Osteocalcin) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
3.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) with multiple changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor) and DAPI diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
3.5 Wash with PBST with multiple changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching and Storage
4.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 0.5% N-butyldiethanolamine in water, RI=1.52) diluted in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
4.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-R+ without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
4.3 Incubation with fresh 100% CUBIC-R+ for final clearing and pre-imaging storage. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor, TH (酪氨酸羟化酶)+Alexa Fluor, CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor]
**Justification:** PEGASOS is specifically optimized for hard tissues like bones and teeth. It incorporates a decalcification step that allows deep penetration of antibodies into the mineralized dental hard tissue and renders both the tooth structure and the soft dental pulp highly transparent. PGP9.5 and TH (酪氨酸羟化酶) are selected to distinguish pan-nerve and sympathetic nerve fibers, respectively, while CD31 (PECAM1) serves as the vascular endothelial marker. Alexa Fluor dyes provide robust, multiplexable fluorescence that is well-preserved in the PEGASOS clearing medium.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Decalcification and Decolorization (Pre-processing)
1.1 Incubation with 20% (w/v) EDTA aqueous solution (pH 7.4) for decalcification. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days)
1.2 Wash with PBS to remove excess EDTA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
1.3 Incubation with 25% (v/v) Quadrol aqueous solution for decolorization. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
1.4 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

2 Immunolabeling
2.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (10% v/v normal serum, 0.5% v/v Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies (PGP9.5, TH (酪氨酸羟化酶), CD31 (PECAM1)) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
2.3 Wash with washing buffer (PBS with 0.1% v/v Tween-20). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor series) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)
2.5 Wash with washing buffer (PBS with 0.1% v/v Tween-20). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Delipidation and Dehydration

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD3+Alexa Fluor, CD8+Alexa Fluor, DAPI]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly effective for dense, lipid-rich tissues like human skin. Crucially, its methanol/H2O2 bleaching step efficiently reduces the high melanin pigment background, which is essential for this specific problem statement. The method provides excellent preservation of Alexa Fluor dyes and deep penetration for antibodies, allowing clear 3D visualization and differentiation of CD3+ (pan-T cell) and CD8+ (cytotoxic T cell) populations at the epidermal/dermal junction.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Pre-treatment and Melanin Bleaching
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.7 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes methanol) for melanin bleaching. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.8 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.9 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.10 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.11 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.12 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.13 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Permeabilization and Blocking
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 20% DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 6% Donkey Serum in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

3 Immunolabeling
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies (anti-CD3 and anti-CD8) diluted in PtHw buffer (PBS with 0.2% Tween-20 and 10 µg/ml heparin) containing 5% DMSO and 3% Donkey Serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
3.2 Wash with PtHw buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.3 Wash with PtHw buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.4 Wash with PtHw buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.5 Wash with PtHw buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.6 Wash with PtHw buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 16 hours)
3.7 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor conjugated) and DAPI diluted in PtHw buffer containing 3% Donkey Serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
3.8 Wash with PtHw buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.9 Wash with PtHw buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.10 Wash with PtHw buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.11 Wash with PtHw buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.12 Wash with PtHw buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 16 hours)

4 Tissue Optical Clearing and RI Matching
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.7 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) and 33% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
4.8 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.9 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.10 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI = 1.56) for refractive index matching and storage prior to imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
